units.zh: 輿服上
units.en: Carriages and Clothing, Part One
units.literal: Carriages and clothing, part one

units.zh: 天子車輅、皇后妃嬪車輦、皇太子車制、王公以下車制及鞍勒飾
units.en: The Emperor's State Carriages; Palanquins for the Empress and Consorts; Regulations for the Crown Prince's Carriage; Carriage Regulations for Princes, Dukes, and Those of Lower Rank; and Ornamentation for Saddles and Bridles
units.literal: The Son of Heaven's carriages and chariots; the empress's and consorts' palanquins; the crown prince's carriage regulations; carriage regulations for princes, dukes, and those below; and saddle and bridle ornamentation

units.zh: 古者軍輿之制，各有名物表識，以祀以封，以田以戎，所以別上下、明等威也。
units.en: In antiquity, regulations governing military carriages assigned distinct names and identifying insignia to each type, whether for sacrifice, enfeoffment, the hunt, or war—so that rank and authority could be clearly distinguished.
units.literal: In antiquity the regulations for military carriages each had named objects and identifying marks, for sacrifice and for enfeoffment, for the hunt and for war—thereby to distinguish superior and inferior and to make clear rank and authority.

units.zh: 歷代相承，互有損益，或因時創始，或襲舊致文，奇巧日滋，浮靡益蕩。
units.en: Successive dynasties inherited these practices, each altering them here and there; some devised new forms to suit the times, others preserved old models for the sake of display. Ingenuity grew ever more elaborate, and lavish excess spread ever wider.
units.literal: Dynasties handed these down in succession, each adding or reducing something; some created new forms according to the times, others followed old models to achieve ornament; ingenious contrivances grew daily, and extravagant excess swelled ever more.

units.zh: 加以後世便習騎乘，車用蓋寡，惟於郊廟祀享法駕導引，為一代令儀而不敢廢也。
units.en: Later ages moreover grew accustomed to riding horseback, so that carriages fell largely out of use. They survived only in the imperial procession at suburban and temple sacrifices, where they remained the prescribed ceremonial of the dynasty—and even that ritual no one dared abolish.
units.literal: Moreover, in later ages people grew accustomed to riding on horseback, and carriages came to be little used; only at suburban and temple sacrifices, when the imperial procession was led forth, did they remain the prescribed ritual of an age—and even that they did not dare abolish.

units.zh: 其于先王經世立法之意，寥乎闊哉！
units.en: As for the intent of the former kings in establishing institutions to govern the world—that purpose now seems remote indeed.
units.literal: As for the intent of the former kings in establishing institutions to govern the world—how remote and vast it has become!

units.zh: 金初得遼之儀物，既而克宋，於是乎有車輅之制。
units.en: When the Jin first acquired the Liao ceremonial regalia and later conquered the Song, they then established regulations for state carriages.
units.literal: When the Jin first came into possession of the Liao ritual objects, and thereafter conquered the Song, they then had regulations for carriages and chariots.

units.zh: 熙宗幸燕，始用法駕。
units.en: When Emperor Xizong visited Yan, he first employed the full imperial procession.
units.literal: When Emperor Xizong visited Yan, he first employed the imperial procession.

units.zh: 迨至世宗，製作乃定，班班乎古矣！
units.en: By the reign of Emperor Shizong, the specifications were finally settled—splendid indeed, in the manner of antiquity!
units.literal: By the time of Emperor Shizong, the manufacture was fixed, and splendid indeed like the ancients!

units.zh: 考禮文，證國史，以見一代之制度雲。
units.en: By examining ritual texts and verifying them against dynastic histories, one may discern the institutions of the age.
units.literal: Examining ritual texts and verifying against dynastic histories, one may see the institutions of an age.

units.zh: 大定十一年，將有事於南郊，命太常寺檢宋南郊禮，鹵簿當用玉輅、金輅、象輅、革輅、木輅、耕根車、明遠車、指南車、記裏鼓車、崇德車、皮軒車、進賢車、黃鉞車、白鷺車、鸞旗車、豹尾車、軺車、羊車各一，革車五，屬車十二。
units.en: In the eleventh year of Dading [1171], as preparations began for a southern suburban sacrifice, the Directorate of Ceremonial ordered the Office of Imperial Sacrifices to consult the Song ritual for that ceremony. The guard of honor was to include one each of the jade, golden, elephant, leather, and wooden state carriages, along with the plough-root, bright-distance, south-pointing, mile-recording drum, exalting-virtue, tiger-skin, advancing-worthies, yellow battle-axe, white egret, luan-banner, leopard-tail, light, and sheep carriages, five leather war-chariots, and twelve attendant carriages.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading, when a southern suburban sacrifice was to be performed, the Directorate of Ceremonial ordered the Office of Imperial Sacrifices to consult the Song regulations for the southern suburban sacrifice; the guard of honor was to employ one each of the jade carriage, golden carriage, elephant carriage, leather carriage, wooden carriage, plough-root carriage, bright-distance carriage, south-pointing carriage, mile-recording drum carriage, exalting-virtue carriage, tiger-skin carriage, advancing-worthies carriage, yellow battle-axe carriage, white egret carriage, luan-banner carriage, leopard-tail carriage, light carriage, and sheep carriage, five leather war-chariots, and twelve attendant carriages.

units.zh: 除見有車輅外，闕象、木、革輅、耕根、明遠、皮軒、進賢、白鷺、羊車，大輦各一，革車三，屬車四。
units.en: Beyond the carriages already available, the court still lacked one each of the elephant, wooden, and leather state carriages, the plough-root, bright-distance, tiger-skin, advancing-worthies, white egret, and sheep carriages, and the great palanquin, as well as three leather war-chariots and four attendant carriages.
units.literal: Apart from the carriages and chariots already on hand, there were lacking one each of the elephant, wooden, and leather carriages, the plough-root, bright-distance, tiger-skin, advancing-worthies, white egret, and sheep carriages, and the great palanquin, three leather war-chariots, and four attendant carriages.

units.zh: 按《五禮新儀》，玉輅以青，金輅以緋，象輅以銀褐，革輅以黃，木輅以皁，蓋其物有合隨輅之色者，有當用別色者，如玉輅用青絲繡雲龍絡帶，青羅繡寶相花帶，青畫輪轅，青氂牛尾，此隨輅之色者也。
units.en: According to the New Rituals of the Five Ceremonies, the jade carriage was green, the golden carriage scarlet, the elephant carriage silver-brown, the leather carriage yellow, and the wooden carriage black. Some fittings matched the carriage's color; others required a different hue.
units.literal: According to the New Rituals of the Five Ceremonies, the jade carriage used green, the golden carriage scarlet, the elephant carriage silver-brown, the leather carriage yellow, and the wooden carriage black; some objects matched the color of the carriage, while others required a different color.

units.zh: 若象、木、革輅則當用緋、用銀褐、用黃及皁。
units.en: The elephant, wooden, and leather carriages were to use scarlet, silver-brown, yellow, and black respectively.
units.literal: As for the elephant, wooden, and leather carriages, scarlet, silver-brown, yellow, and black were to be used respectively.

units.zh: 若至尊乘禦步武所及，非若餘物但為美觀，其踏床、倚背、踏道之褥皆用紅錦，座褥、及行馬褥、透壁軟簾三，用銀褐、黃、青羅錦三色。
units.en: Where the sovereign himself trod the ground his carriage reached—unlike mere display pieces—the foot-rest, back-rest, and footway cushions were all of red brocade, while seat cushions, railing-barrier cushions, and three sheer hanging curtains used silver-brown, yellow, and green brocade.
units.literal: Where the sovereign himself walked in the places his carriage reached—not like other objects that were merely for display—the foot-rest, back-rest, and footway cushions all used red brocade; seat cushions, railing-barrier cushions, and the three sheer hanging curtains used silver-brown, yellow, and green brocade.

units.zh: 又大輦，宋陶穀創意為之，至祥符中以其太重，減七百餘斤，可見當時亦無定制，各以意從長斟酌造之。
units.en: The great palanquin, moreover, was a Song invention of Tao Gu's; by the Xiangfu reign its weight had been cut by more than seven hundred jin, which shows that even then there was no fixed standard and each was built as convenience dictated.
units.literal: Moreover, the great palanquin was devised on Tao Gu's initiative in the Song; by the Xiangfu era its weight had been reduced by more than seven hundred jin, showing that even then there was no fixed regulation and each was made according to convenience and length.

units.zh: 其制，金玉輅闕，可見者象輅、革輅、木輅，耕根、皮軒、進賢、明遠、白鷺、羊車、革車、大輦，凡十有一：
units.en: Of the full set, the jade and golden carriages were missing; those on record were the elephant, leather, and wooden carriages, the plough-root, tiger-skin, advancing-worthies, bright-distance, white egret, and sheep carriages, leather war-chariots, and great palanquin—eleven types in all:
units.literal: Of the regulations, the jade and golden carriages were lacking; those that could be seen were the elephant, leather, and wooden carriages, the plough-root, tiger-skin, advancing-worthies, bright-distance, white egret, and sheep carriages, leather war-chariots, and great palanquin—eleven in all:

units.zh: 象輅，黃質，金塗銅裝，以象飾諸末。
units.en: Elephant carriage: a yellow body with gilt-bronze fittings, elephant ornamentation at the extremities.
units.literal: Elephant carriage: yellow body, gilt-bronze fittings, with elephant ornament on the extremities.

units.zh: 輪衣以銀褐。
units.en: Wheel covers of silver-brown.
units.literal: Wheel covers in silver-brown.

units.zh: 建大赤。
units.en: It bore a great scarlet banner.
units.literal: It bore a great scarlet banner.

units.zh: 餘同玉輅。
units.en: All else matched the jade carriage.
units.literal: The rest was the same as the jade carriage.

units.zh: 革輅，黃質，鞔之以革，金塗銅裝，輪衣以黃，建大白。
units.en: Leather carriage: yellow body covered in leather with gilt-bronze fittings, yellow wheel covers, and a great white banner.
units.literal: Leather carriage: yellow body, covered with leather, gilt-bronze fittings, wheel covers yellow, bearing a great white banner.

units.zh: 餘同玉輅。
units.en: All else matched the jade carriage.
units.literal: The rest was the same as the jade carriage.

units.zh: 木輅，黑質，漆之，輪衣以皁，建大麾。
units.en: Wooden carriage: black lacquered body, black wheel covers, and a great command banner.
units.literal: Wooden carriage: black body, lacquered, wheel covers black, bearing a great command banner.

units.zh: 餘同玉輅。
units.en: All else matched the jade carriage.
units.literal: The rest was the same as the jade carriage.

units.zh: 耕根車，青質，蓋三重，制如玉輅而無玉飾。
units.en: Plough-root carriage: green body with a triple canopy, built like the jade carriage but without jade ornamentation.
units.literal: Plough-root carriage: green body, triple canopy, made like the jade carriage but without jade ornament.

units.zh: 皮軒車，赤質，上有漆柱，貫五輪相重，畫虎紋，一轅。
units.en: Tiger-skin carriage: red body with lacquered pillars above, five wheels stacked in succession and painted with tiger stripes, one shaft.
units.literal: Tiger-skin carriage: red body, with lacquered pillars above, five wheels stacked one upon another, painted with tiger patterns, one shaft.

units.zh: 進賢車，赤質，如革車，緋輪衣、絡帶、門簾並繡鳳。
units.en: Advancing-worthies carriage: red body like the leather war-chariot, with scarlet wheel covers, belt bands, and door curtains all embroidered with phoenixes.
units.literal: Advancing-worthies carriage: red body, like the leather war-chariot, with scarlet wheel covers, belt bands, and door curtains all embroidered with phoenixes.

units.zh: 上設硃漆床、香案，紫綾衣。
units.en: It carried a vermilion-lacquered couch and incense table with purple damask covers.
units.literal: Above it were set a vermilion-lacquered couch and incense table, with purple damask covers.

units.zh: 一轅。
units.en: One shaft.
units.literal: One shaft.

units.zh: 明遠車，制如屋，銳頂，重簷，勾欄。
units.en: Bright-distance carriage: built like a house with a pointed roof, double eaves, and balustrades.
units.literal: Bright-distance carriage: shaped like a house, with pointed top, double eaves, and balustrades.

units.zh: 頂上有金龍，四角垂鐸。
units.en: A gilt dragon crowned the roof; bells hung from the four corners.
units.literal: On the top was a gilt dragon; from the four corners hung bells.

units.zh: 上層四面垂簾，下層周以花板。
units.en: The upper story had curtains on all four sides; the lower was ringed with patterned panels.
units.literal: The upper story had curtains hanging on all four sides; the lower story was encircled with patterned panels.

units.zh: 三轅。
units.en: Three shafts.
units.literal: Three shafts.

units.zh: 白鷺車，赤質，周施花板，上有漆柱，柱杪刻為鷺鷥，銜鵝毛筒，紅綬帶。
units.en: White egret carriage: red body ringed with patterned panels, lacquered pillars above carved at the tips as egrets holding goose-feather tubes bound with red silk cords.
units.literal: White egret carriage: red body, patterned panels all around, with lacquered pillars above; the pillar tips were carved as egrets holding goose-feather tubes with red silk cords.

units.zh: 柱貫五輪相重。
units.en: The pillars passed through five wheels stacked in succession.
units.literal: The pillars passed through five wheels stacked one upon another.

units.zh: 輪衣、皁頂、緋裙、緋絡帶，並繡飛鷺。
units.en: Wheel covers, black canopy top, scarlet skirt, and scarlet belt bands were all embroidered with flying egrets.
units.literal: Wheel covers, black canopy top, scarlet skirt, and scarlet belt bands were all embroidered with flying egrets.

units.zh: 一轅。
units.en: One shaft.
units.literal: One shaft.

units.zh: 羊車，赤質，兩壁油畫龜紋，金鳳翅，幰衣、結帶並繡瑞羊。
units.en: Sheep carriage: red body with both side panels oil-painted with tortoise patterns, gilt phoenix wings, and canopy cover and knotted bands embroidered with auspicious sheep.
units.literal: Sheep carriage: red body, both side panels painted in oil with tortoise patterns, gilt phoenix wings, canopy cover and knotted bands all embroidered with auspicious sheep.

units.zh: 二轅。
units.en: Two shafts.
units.literal: Two shafts.

units.zh: 大輦，赤質，正方，油畫，金塗銀葉龍鳳裝。
units.en: Great palanquin: red square body, oil-painted, with gilt silver-leaf dragon and phoenix fittings.
units.literal: Great palanquin: red body, square, oil-painted, with gilt silver-leaf dragon and phoenix fittings.

units.zh: 其上四面施行龍、雲朵、火珠，方鑒、銀絲囊網，珠翠結雲龍，鈿窠霞子。
units.en: Above on all four sides were traveling dragons, cloud clusters, fire pearls, square mirrors, silver-thread net pouches, pearl-and-jade knotted cloud-dragons, and inlaid rosettes.
units.literal: On all four sides above were traveling dragons, cloud clusters, fire pearls, square mirrors, silver-thread net pouches, pearl-and-jade knotted cloud-dragons, and inlaid rosettes.

units.zh: 四角龍頭銜香囊。
units.en: Dragon heads at the four corners held incense pouches.
units.literal: At the four corners dragon heads held incense pouches.

units.zh: 頂輪施耀葉，中有銀蓮花，坐龍。
units.en: Radiant leaves adorned the crown wheel; within stood a silver lotus bearing a seated dragon.
units.literal: Radiant leaves were set on the crown wheel; within was a silver lotus with a seated dragon.

units.zh: 紅綾裏，碧牙壓帖。
units.en: The lining was red damask with green ivory pressure strips.
units.literal: Red damask lining, with green ivory pressure strips.

units.zh: 內設圓鑒、香囊，銀飾勾欄台坐，紫絲條網帉錔。
units.en: Inside were a round mirror and incense pouch, a silver-fitted balustrade platform seat, and purple silk net fringe clasps.
units.literal: Within were set a round mirror and incense pouch, with silver-fitted balustrade platform seat and purple silk net fringe clasps.

units.zh: 中施黃褥，上置御座、曲幾，香爐、錦結綬。
units.en: A yellow cushion was laid within, bearing the imperial seat and curved armrest, an incense burner, and brocade knotted cords.
units.literal: A yellow cushion was laid within, with imperial seat and curved armrest, incense burner, and brocade knotted cords.

units.zh: 幾衣、輪衣、絡帶並緋繡雲龍寶相花，金線壓。
units.en: Armrest cover, wheel cover, and belt bands were all scarlet-embroidered with cloud-dragons and treasure-floral patterns pressed in gold thread.
units.literal: Armrest cover, wheel cover, and belt bands were all scarlet-embroidered cloud-dragons and treasure-floral patterns with gold thread pressing.

units.zh: 長竿四，飾以金塗銀龍頭。
units.en: Four long poles ornamented with gilt silver dragon heads.
units.literal: Four long poles, ornamented with gilt silver dragon heads.

units.zh: 畫梯、托叉、行馬。
units.en: Painted ladder, carrying forks, and railing barriers.
units.literal: Painted ladder, carrying forks, and railing barriers.

units.zh: 七寶輦，制如大輦，飾以玉裙網，七寶，滴子用真珠。
units.en: Seven-treasure palanquin: built like the great palanquin and ornamented with jade skirt nets and the seven treasures; its drip beads were of genuine pearl.
units.literal: Seven-treasure palanquin: made like the great palanquin, ornamented with jade skirt nets and the seven treasures; the drip beads used genuine pearls.

units.zh: 宋欽宗為上皇制，海陵自汴取而用之。
units.en: Emperor Qinzong of the Song had it made for the Retired Emperor; Prince Hailing took it from Bian and put it to use.
units.literal: Emperor Qinzong of the Song had it made for the Retired Emperor; Hailing took it from Bian and used it.

units.zh: 皇后之車六。
units.en: The empress had six carriages.
units.literal: The empress had six carriages.

units.zh: 一曰重翟車，青質，金飾金塗銅鈒花葉段裝釘，燿葉二十四，明金立鳳一，紫羅銷金生色寶相帷一，青羅、青油幰衣各一，硃絲絡網、紫羅明金生色雲龍絡帶各二，兩廂明金五彩間裝翟羽二，金塗鍮石長轅鳳頭三，橫轅立鸞八，香爐香寶子一副，宜男錦帶結，硃紅漆杌子、踏床各一，扶板扶魚一副，紅羅明金衣褥，紅羅襯褥一，青羅行道褥四，青羅明金生色雲鳳夾幔一，紅羅明金緣紅竹簾二，金塗銅葉段行馬二，硃紅漆金塗銀葉裝釘胡梯一，青羅胡梯尋儀褥二，踏道褥十，青絹裹大麻索二，油蒙帕一。
units.en: First, the Heavy-Pheasant carriage: green body with gold ornament and gilt-bronze chased floral fittings, twenty-four radiant leaves, one standing gilt phoenix, purple brocade polychrome treasure-floral curtains, green brocade and green oil canopy covers, vermilion silk nets and purple brocade polychrome cloud-dragon belt bands, polychrome gold pheasant-feather side panels, gilt pewter long-shaft phoenix heads, eight standing pheasants on the cross-shaft, incense burner and treasure, propitious-male brocade knots, vermilion-lacquered stool and foot-rest, hand boards and hand fish, red brocade polychrome cushions and linings, green brocade traveling and side curtains, red bamboo curtains with gold edges, gilt-bronze railing barriers, foreign ladder and attendant cushions, footway cushions, hemp ropes in green silk, and oil-cloth wrapping—each in the quantities prescribed.
units.literal: The first was called the Heavy-Pheasant carriage: green body, gold ornament and gilt-bronze chased floral-leaf segment fittings and nails, twenty-four radiant leaves, one standing gilt phoenix, one purple brocade gold-cut polychrome treasure-floral curtain, one each of green brocade and green oil canopy cover, two each of vermilion silk net and purple brocade polychrome gold-cut cloud-dragon belt bands, two pheasant-feather panels with polychrome gold fittings on both sides, three gilt pewter long-shaft phoenix heads, eight standing pheasants on the cross-shaft, one set of incense burner and incense treasure, knotted with propitious-male brocade bands, one each of vermilion-lacquered stool and foot-rest, one set of hand boards and hand fish, red brocade polychrome gold garment-cushion, one red brocade lining cushion, four green brocade traveling cushions, one green brocade polychrome gold-cut cloud-phoenix side curtain, two red brocade polychrome gold-edged red bamboo curtains, two gilt-bronze leaf-segment railing barriers, one vermilion-lacquered gilt silver-leaf fitted nail foreign ladder, two green brocade foreign-ladder attendant cushions, ten footway cushions, two green silk-wrapped hemp ropes, one oil-cloth wrapping.

units.zh: 二曰厭翟車，赤質，倒仙錦帷一，紫羅、紫油幰衣各一，硃絲絡網，宜男錦絡帶各二，余同重翟，惟行道褥、夾幔、尋儀褥羅及裹索等用紅。
units.en: Second, the Averted-Pheasant carriage: red body with an inverted-immortal brocade curtain, purple brocade and purple oil canopy covers, and vermilion silk nets and propitious-male brocade belt bands; otherwise as the Heavy-Pheasant, but traveling cushions, side curtains, attendant cushions, and wrapping ropes were red.
units.literal: The second was called the Averted-Pheasant carriage: red body, one inverted-immortal brocade curtain, one each of purple brocade and purple oil canopy cover, two each of vermilion silk net and propitious-male brocade belt bands; the rest was the same as the Heavy-Pheasant, except traveling cushions, side curtains, attendant cushions, and wrapping ropes were red.

units.zh: 三曰翟車，黃質，金飾鍮石葉段裝釘，宜男錦帷，黃羅油幰衣，鍮石長轅鳳頭三，而無橫轅立鸞，余同厭翟，而羅色用黃。
units.en: Third, the Pheasant carriage: yellow body with gold and pewter fittings, propitious-male brocade curtain, yellow brocade oil canopy cover, three pewter long-shaft phoenix heads but no cross-shaft pheasants; otherwise as the Averted-Pheasant, in yellow.
units.literal: The third was called the Pheasant carriage: yellow body, gold ornament and pewter leaf-segment fittings and nails, propitious-male brocade curtain, yellow brocade oil canopy cover, three pewter long-shaft phoenix heads but no standing pheasants on the cross-shaft; the rest as the Averted-Pheasant, but brocade colors were yellow.

units.zh: 四曰安車，赤質，倒仙錦帷，紫、油幰衣，硃絲絡網，天下樂錦絡帶，鍮石長轅鳳頭三，無橫轅立鸞及香爐香寶子，余同翟車，而色皆用紅。
units.en: Fourth, the Peace carriage: red body with inverted-immortal brocade curtain, purple and oil canopy covers, vermilion silk net, All-under-Heaven-Rejoices brocade belt bands, three pewter phoenix heads, but no cross-shaft pheasants or incense fittings; otherwise as the Pheasant carriage, all in red.
units.literal: The fourth was called the Peace carriage: red body, inverted-immortal brocade curtain, purple and oil canopy covers, vermilion silk net, All-under-Heaven-Rejoices brocade belt bands, three pewter long-shaft phoenix heads, without cross-shaft pheasants or incense burner and treasure; the rest as the Pheasant carriage, but all colors red.

units.zh: 五曰四望車，硃質，宜男錦帷，青、油幰衣，轅端螭頭二，余並同安車。
units.en: Fifth, the Four-Outlook carriage: vermilion body with propitious-male brocade curtain, green and oil canopy covers, two dragon heads at the shaft ends; otherwise as the Peace carriage.
units.literal: The fifth was called the Four-Outlook carriage: vermilion body, propitious-male brocade curtain, green and oil canopy covers, two dragon heads at the shaft ends; the rest all as the Peace carriage.

units.zh: 六曰金根車，硃質，紫羅、紫油幰衣，硃絲絡網、倒仙錦絡帶各二，踏床衣褥用紅綾，尋儀褥、踏道褥並用綾，余並同安車。
units.en: Sixth, the Golden-Root carriage: vermilion body with purple brocade and purple oil canopy covers, vermilion silk nets and inverted-immortal brocade belt bands; foot-rest cushions in red damask, attendant and footway cushions in damask; otherwise as the Peace carriage.
units.literal: The sixth was called the Golden-Root carriage: vermilion body, purple brocade and purple oil canopy covers, two each of vermilion silk net and inverted-immortal brocade belt bands; foot-rest garments and cushions used red damask, attendant and footway cushions used damask; the rest all as the Peace carriage.

units.zh: 造六車成後，複改造圓輅、重簷，方輅、五華、亭頭、平頭六等之制，又增制九龍車一，高二丈、廣一丈一尺、長二丈六尺。
units.en: Once the six carriages were finished, the court revised the round, double-eaved, square, five-flower, pavilion-top, and level-top types and added one Nine-Dragons carriage, two zhang high, one zhang one chi wide, and two zhang six chi long.
units.literal: After the six carriages were completed, they again revised the regulations for the round carriage, double-eaved, square carriage, five-flower, pavilion-top, and level-top types, and additionally made one Nine-Dragons carriage, two zhang in height, one zhang one chi in width, and two zhang six chi in length.

units.zh: 五鳳車四，各高一丈八尺，長廣如之。
units.en: Four Five-Phoenix carriages, each one zhang eight chi high with matching length and width.
units.literal: Five-Phoenix carriages, four in number, each one zhang eight chi high, with length and width proportionate.

units.zh: 圓輅車一、方輅車一、重簷車一，各高一丈七尺，長一丈八尺，廣八尺。
units.en: One round carriage, one square carriage, and one double-eaved carriage, each one zhang seven chi high, one zhang eight chi long, and eight chi wide.
units.literal: One round carriage, one square carriage, and one double-eaved carriage, each one zhang seven chi high, one zhang eight chi long, and eight chi wide.

units.zh: 皆駕馬四，駕士各五十人，並平巾幘、生色青緋黃三色寶相花衫、銀褐抹帶、大口袴。
units.en: Each was drawn by four horses with fifty grooms apiece, in plain headcloths, polychrome green, scarlet, and yellow treasure-floral shirts, silver-brown waist bands, and loose trousers.
units.literal: All were drawn by four horses, with fifty grooms each, wearing plain headcloths, polychrome green-scarlet-yellow treasure-floral shirts, silver-brown waist bands, and loose trousers.

units.zh: 平頭輦一、五華輦一、亭頭輦一，各高一丈九尺，廣丈五寸，長三丈。
units.en: One level-top, one five-flower, and one pavilion-top palanquin, each one zhang nine chi high, one zhang five cun wide, and three zhang long.
units.literal: One level-top palanquin, one five-flower palanquin, and one pavilion-top palanquin, each one zhang nine chi high, one zhang five cun wide, and three zhang long.

units.zh: 舁士各九十六人作兩番代，並生色緋寶相花衫，餘如前制。
units.en: Ninety-six bearers served in two relays, all in polychrome scarlet treasure-floral shirts; other fittings followed the earlier specifications.
units.literal: Ninety-six bearers each worked in two relays, all in polychrome scarlet treasure-floral shirts; the rest as in the previous regulations.

units.zh: 管押人員三十五人，長腳襆頭、紫羅窄衫、金銅帶束。
units.en: Thirty-five supervising officers wore long-foot headwraps, narrow purple brocade shirts, and gilt-copper belts.
units.literal: Thirty-five supervising personnel, with long-foot headwraps, narrow purple brocade shirts, and gilt-copper belt bindings.

units.zh: 駕馬繁纓、涼屜、鈴拂、包尾皆從車色，金銅面，插翟尾，硃轡，硃總。
units.en: Harness plumes, cool saddles, bells, whiskers, and tail wraps matched each carriage's color, with gilt-copper cheekpieces, inserted pheasant-tail plumes, and vermilion bridles and browbands.
units.literal: For the carriage horses, plumes, cool saddles, bells, whiskers, and tail wraps all followed the carriage color, with gilt-copper faces, pheasant-tail plumes inserted, vermilion bridles and vermilion browbands.

units.zh: 龍車合用紅羅傘一，傘子二人用本服錦帽襆帶。
units.en: The dragon carriage required one red brocade umbrella; its two bearers wore their service brocade caps and wrapped belts.
units.literal: For the dragon carriage collectively one red brocade umbrella was used; the two umbrella bearers wore their service brocade caps and wrapped belts.

units.zh: 又檢定扇、障等制。
units.en: Regulations for fans, screens, and related items were also verified.
units.literal: They also verified the regulations for fans, screens, and the like.

units.zh: 偏扇如仙人羽扇。
units.en: Side fans resembled immortal feather fans.
units.literal: Side fans were like immortal feather fans.

units.zh: 行障六扇，各長八尺、高六尺，用紅羅表、硃裏，畫雲鳳，龍首竿銜鞶結，每障用宮人四。
units.en: Traveling screens had six panels, each eight chi long and six chi high, red brocade outside and vermilion within, painted with cloud-phoenixes on dragon-head poles with belt knots; four palace women attended each screen.
units.literal: Traveling screens, six panels, each eight chi long and six chi high, with red brocade outside and vermilion inside, painted with cloud-phoenixes; dragon-head poles held belt knots; four palace women per screen.

units.zh: 坐障三扇，各長七尺、高五尺，畫雲鳳，紅羅表、硃裏，余同行障。
units.en: Seated screens had three panels, each seven chi long and five chi high, painted with cloud-phoenixes in red brocade and vermilion lining, otherwise as the traveling screens.
units.literal: Seated screens, three panels, each seven chi long and five chi high, painted with cloud-phoenixes, red brocade outside and vermilion inside; the rest as the traveling screens.

units.zh: 錦六柱八扇，各闊二尺、高三尺，冒以錦，內給使八人執。
units.en: Brocade six-pillar eight-fan sets were two chi wide and three chi high, brocade-covered, and carried by eight inner attendants.
units.literal: Brocade six-pillar eight-fan sets, each two chi wide and three chi high, covered in brocade; eight inner attendants carried them.

units.zh: 宮人車制如屬車，駕士八人，平巾幘、緋衫、大口袴、鞋襪、供奉宮人三十人，雲腳紗帽、紫衫束帶，綠靴。
units.en: Palace women's carriages followed attendant-carriage regulations: eight grooms in plain headcloths, scarlet shirts, loose trousers, and shoes; thirty attending palace women in cloud-heel gauze caps, purple belted shirts, and green boots.
units.literal: Palace women's carriages were regulated like attendant carriages, with eight grooms in plain headcloths, scarlet shirts, loose trousers, shoes and socks; thirty attending palace women in cloud-heel gauze caps, purple shirts with belts, and green boots.

units.zh: 明昌元年三月，定妃嬪車輦同鍍金鳳頭、黃結。
units.en: In the third month of the first year of Mingchang [1190], consorts' palanquins were standardized to gilt phoenix heads and yellow knots.
units.literal: In the third month of the first year of Mingchang, it was fixed that consorts' palanquins should use the same gilt phoenix head and yellow knots.

units.zh: 禦妻、世婦用間金鳳頭、梅紅結子。
units.en: Imperial wives and court ladies used mixed-gold phoenix heads and plum-red knots.
units.literal: Imperial wives and court ladies used mixed-gold phoenix heads and plum-red knots.

units.zh: 皇太子車制。
units.en: Regulations for the Crown Prince's Carriage
units.literal: Regulations for the crown prince's carriage.

units.zh: 大定六年十二月，奏皇太子金輅典故制度，及上用金輅儀式，奉敕詳定。
units.en: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Dading [1166], officials memorialized on precedents for the crown prince's golden carriage and on the emperor's golden-carriage ceremony; the throne ordered a detailed determination.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Dading, a memorial was submitted on the crown prince's golden carriage precedents and regulations, and on the ceremonial for the emperor's use of the golden carriage; an imperial order directed detailed determination.

units.zh: 輈、旗、旂首及應用龍者更以麟為飾，省去障塵等物。
units.en: Shafts, banners, banner heads, and all dragon motifs were to use unicorn ornament instead; dust screens and similar items were to be omitted.
units.literal: Shafts, banners, banner heads, and wherever dragons were used were to be changed to unicorn ornament; dust screens and similar objects were to be removed.

units.zh: 上用金輅名件色數，依上公以九為節，減四分之一。
units.en: For the named items and colors of the emperor's golden carriage, following the upper duke's standard of nine as the measure, one quarter was to be reduced.
units.literal: For items and colors on the emperor's golden carriage, following the upper duke's standard of nine as the measure, one quarter was to be reduced.

units.zh: 上用輅，軾前有金龍改為伏鹿，軾上坐龍改為鳳，旂十二旒減為九，駕赤騮六減為四，及簾褥用黃羅處改用梅紅，余並具體成造。
units.en: On the imperial model, the golden dragon before the railing became a crouching deer, the seated railing dragon a phoenix, twelve banner tassels became nine, six scarlet bays four; yellow brocade curtains and cushions became plum-red; all else was to be built to full specification.
units.literal: On the emperor's carriage, the golden dragon before the railing was changed to a crouching deer, the seated dragon on the railing to a phoenix, twelve banner tassels reduced to nine, six scarlet bays reduced to four; wherever yellow brocade was used for curtains and cushions, plum-red was used instead; the rest was to be fully manufactured in concrete form.

units.zh: 其制，赤質，金飾諸末，重較。
units.en: Specifications: red body, gold ornamentation at the extremities, double curved side rails.
units.literal: Its regulation: red body, gold ornament on the extremities, double curved sides.

units.zh: 箱畫虞文鳥獸，黃屋。
units.en: The carriage box painted with Yu-pattern birds and beasts, with a yellow canopy.
units.literal: The box painted with Yu-pattern birds and beasts, yellow canopy.

units.zh: 軾作赤伏鹿，龍輈。
units.en: The railing bore a scarlet crouching deer, with dragon shafts.
units.literal: The railing made a scarlet crouching deer, with dragon shafts.

units.zh: 金鳳一，在軾前。
units.en: One gilt phoenix before the railing.
units.literal: One gilt phoenix, set before the railing.

units.zh: 設障塵。
units.en: A dust screen was fitted.
units.literal: A dust screen was set.

units.zh: 硃蓋黃裏。
units.en: Vermilion canopy with yellow lining.
units.literal: Vermilion canopy with yellow lining.

units.zh: 輪畫硃牙。
units.en: Wheels painted with vermilion spokes.
units.literal: Wheels painted with vermilion spokes.

units.zh: 左建九旒，右載闟戟。
units.en: Nine tassels were raised on the left; the halberd of authority was mounted on the right.
units.literal: On the left nine tassels were set up; on the right the halberd of authority was loaded.

units.zh: 旂首銜金龍頭，結綏及鈴緌。
units.en: The banner head bore a gilt dragon head with knotted cords and bell tassels.
units.literal: The banner head held a gilt dragon head, with knotted cords and bell tassels.

units.zh: 八鸞在衡，二鈴在軾。
units.en: Eight luan bells on the crossbar, two on the railing.
units.literal: Eight luan bells on the crossbar, two bells on the railing.

units.zh: 駕赤騮四，金勣釳方，插翟尾，鏤錫鞶，纓九就。
units.en: Drawn by four scarlet bays with gilt patterned plaques, inserted pheasant-tail plumes, carved tin bridles, and nine-part throat tassels.
units.literal: Drawn by four scarlet bays, with gilt patterned square plaques, pheasant-tail plumes inserted, carved tin bridles, and nine-part throat tassels.

units.zh: 皇帝輅自頂至地高一丈七尺，今閷四分之一為一丈三尺二寸，修廣之閷亦如之。
units.en: The emperor's carriage stood one zhang seven chi from crown to ground; one quarter was cut away, yielding one zhang three chi two cun, with length and width reduced proportionally.
units.literal: The emperor's carriage from crown to ground was one zhang seven chi high; now one quarter was cut off, making one zhang three chi two cun; length and width were reduced proportionally.

units.zh: 王公以下車制。
units.en: Carriage Regulations for Princes, Dukes, and Those of Lower Rank
units.literal: Carriage regulations for princes, dukes, and those below.

units.zh: 一品，轅用銀螭頭，涼棚杆子、月板並許以銀裝飾。
units.en: First rank: shafts might use silver dragon heads; cool-awning poles and moon boards might all be ornamented in silver.
units.literal: First rank: shafts used silver dragon heads; cool-awning poles and moon boards were all permitted silver ornament.

units.zh: 三品以上，螭頭不得施銀，涼棚杆子、月板亦聽用銀為飾。
units.en: Third rank and above: dragon heads might not be silvered, but cool-awning poles and moon boards might still use silver ornament.
units.literal: Third rank and above: dragon heads might not use silver, but cool-awning poles and moon boards were permitted silver ornament.

units.zh: 五品以上，轅獅頭。
units.en: Fifth rank and above: lion heads on the shafts.
units.literal: Fifth rank and above: lion heads on the shafts.

units.zh: 六品以下，轅雲頭。
units.en: Sixth rank and below: cloud heads on the shafts.
units.literal: Sixth rank and below: cloud heads on the shafts.

units.zh: 庶人坐車平頭，止用一色黑油。
units.en: Commoners' riding carriages had level tops and used only black oil in a single color.
units.literal: Commoners' riding carriages had level tops and used only one color of black oil.

units.zh: 親王鞍，塗金銀裹，仍鈒以開花。
units.en: Princes' saddles were coated and wrapped in gilt silver and chased with openwork floral patterns.
units.literal: Princes' saddles were coated and wrapped in gilt silver, still chased with openwork flowers.

units.zh: 障泥用紫羅，飾以錦。
units.en: Mud-guards were of purple brocade ornamented with brocade.
units.literal: Mud-guards used purple brocade, ornamented with brocade.

units.zh: 轡以塗金銀裝，束用絲結。
units.en: Bridles were wrapped in gilt silver and bound with silk knots.
units.literal: Bridles were wrapped in gilt silver, bound with silk knots.

units.zh: 皇家小功以上、太皇太后皇太后大功以上、皇后期親以上、並一品官、及官職俱至三品以上者，障泥許用金花。
units.en: Members of the imperial clan from lesser merit mourning upward, the Grand and Regular Empress Dowagers from greater merit mourning upward, the empress from close kin upward, and first-rank officials—or those whose offices all reached third rank and above—might use gold floral patterns on mud-guards.
units.literal: For the imperial clan from lesser merit mourning upward, for the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager from greater merit mourning upward, for the empress from close kin upward, and for first-rank officials and those whose offices all reached third rank and above, mud-guards were permitted to use gold floral patterns.

units.zh: 若經賜或禦球場內，不在禁限。
units.en: Items bestowed by imperial grant or used within the imperial ball ground were exempt from these restrictions.
units.literal: If bestowed by imperial grant or within the imperial ball ground, they were not within the prohibition.

units.zh: 舊制，親王、宰執任外者，與大興尹，皆服小帽、束帶、銀鞍、絲鞭。
units.en: Formerly, princes and chief ministers posted outside the capital, along with the Daxing magistrate, all wore small caps, belt bindings, silver saddles, and silk whips.
units.literal: Under the old regulations, when princes and chief ministers served outside the capital, together with the Daxing magistrate, all wore small caps, belt bindings, silver saddles, and silk whips.

units.zh: 大定中，世宗以京尹亦外官三品，而與親王無別，遂命不得禦銀鞍、絲鞭，惟同外三品例，襆頭、帶、展皁視事。
units.en: During Dading, Emperor Shizong ruled that the capital magistrate, though a third-rank outside post, should not share princely privileges; he was barred from silver saddles and silk whips and followed the outside-third-rank norm of headwrap, belt, and black boots for official business.
units.literal: In the Dading era Emperor Shizong held that the capital magistrate, though also an outside official of third rank, should not be treated like princes, and ordered that he might not use silver saddles or silk whips but only follow the outside-third-rank precedent of headwrap, belt, and black boots for conducting affairs.

units.zh: 承安二年，制護衛銅裝鞍轡不得借人。
units.en: In the second year of Cheng'an [1197], guard-service copper-fitted saddles and bridles were forbidden to be lent out.
units.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an, it was decreed that guard-service copper-fitted saddles and bridles might not be lent to others.

units.zh: 庶人馬鞍許用黑漆，以骨、角、鐵為飾，不得用玉較具及金、銀、犀、象飾鞍轡。
units.en: Commoners' saddles might use black lacquer with bone, horn, or iron ornament, but not jade cheekpieces or gold, silver, rhinoceros, or ivory fittings.
units.literal: Commoners' horse saddles were permitted black lacquer, with bone, horn, and iron for ornament, but might not use jade cheekpieces or gold, silver, rhinoceros, or ivory saddle and bridle ornament.

units.zh: 輿服中
units.en: Carriages and Clothing, Part Two
units.literal: Carriages and clothing, part two

units.zh: 天子袞冕
units.en: The Emperor's Robe and Crown
units.literal: The Son of Heaven's robe and crown

units.zh: 昔者聖人制為玄黃黼黻之服，以象天地之德，以章貴賤之儀，夏、商損益，至周大備，不可以有加矣。
units.en: In antiquity the sages devised garments in black, yellow, and fu-and-fu patterns to symbolize the virtues of Heaven and Earth and to mark noble and base rank. Xia and Shang altered them; by Zhou the system was complete and could not be improved upon.
units.literal: In antiquity the sages made garments of black, yellow, fu, and fu patterns to symbolize the virtue of Heaven and Earth and to display the ritual of noble and base; Xia and Shang added and reduced, until Zhou made them complete—nothing more could be added.

units.zh: 自秦滅棄禮法，先王之制靡敝不存，漢初猶服袀玄以從大祀，歷代雖漸復古，終亦不純而已。
units.en: When Qin abolished ritual law, the institutions of former kings were largely lost. Early Han still wore dark garments for major sacrifices; later dynasties gradually restored antiquity, yet never fully recovered the original purity.
units.literal: From Qin's destruction and abandonment of ritual law, the former kings' regulations were worn away until none survived; at the beginning of Han they still wore dark garments for great sacrifices; though later dynasties gradually restored antiquity, in the end they were never pure.

units.zh: 金制皇帝服通天、絳紗、兗冕、逼，即前代之遺制也。
units.en: Jin imperial dress included the penetration-heaven cap, scarlet gauze robe, Yan crown, and Bi cap—forms inherited from earlier dynasties.
units.literal: Under Jin regulations the emperor's dress included the penetration-heaven, scarlet gauze, Yan crown, and Bi—survivals of earlier dynasties' institutions.

units.zh: 其臣有貂蟬法服，即所謂朝服者。
units.en: Ministers wore sable-tail ceremonial dress—the so-called court dress.
units.literal: His ministers had sable-tail ceremonial dress, namely what was called court dress.

units.zh: 章宗時，禮官請參酌漢、唐，更制祭服，青衣硃裳，去貂蟬豎筆，以別於朝服。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhangzong, ritual officials proposed following Han and Tang to redesign sacrificial dress as green upper garment and vermilion skirt, omitting sable tail and upright brush to distinguish it from court dress.
units.literal: In Emperor Zhangzong's time ritual officials requested reference to Han and Tang to remake sacrificial dress: green upper garment and vermilion skirt, removing sable tail and upright brush to distinguish it from court dress.

units.zh: 惟公朝則又有紫、緋、綠三等之服，與夫窄紫、展皁等事，悉著於篇雲。
units.en: For routine audiences there were also purple, scarlet, and green grades of dress, along with narrow purple and spread-black boots—all recorded in this chapter.
units.literal: For public audiences there were also purple, scarlet, and green grades of dress, and matters such as narrow purple and spread-black boots—all are set down in this chapter.

units.zh: 天眷三年，有司以車駕將幸燕京，合用通天冠、絳紗袍，據見闕名件，依式成造。
units.en: In the third year of Tianjuan [1140], as the court prepared for the imperial visit to Yanjing, officials supplied the penetration-heaven cap and scarlet gauze robe, manufacturing missing pieces to specification.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianjuan, when offices prepared for the imperial progress to Yanjing, the penetration-heaven cap and scarlet gauze robe were required; according to missing named items, they were made to pattern.

units.zh: 禮服，袍、裳、方心曲領、中單、蔽膝、革帶、大帶、玉具劍、綬、佩、褵、襪。
units.en: Ceremonial dress comprised robe, skirt, square-heart curved collar, inner garment, knee cover, leather belt, great belt, jade-fitted sword, cord, pendant, shoes, and socks.
units.literal: Ceremonial dress: robe, skirt, square-heart curved collar, inner garment, knee cover, leather belt, great belt, jade-fitted sword, cord, pendant, shoes, and socks.

units.zh: 乘輿服，大綬六采，黑、黃、赤、白、縹、綠、小綬三色，同大綬，間施三玉環，大綬五百首，小綬半之。
units.en: Imperial cords included a great six-color cord of black, yellow, scarlet, white, light blue, and green, and a three-color small cord matching it with three jade rings between; the great cord had five hundred tassels, the small cord half as many.
units.literal: Imperial dress: great cord of six colors—black, yellow, scarlet, white, light blue, and green; small cord of three colors matching the great cord, with three jade rings set between; the great cord had five hundred tassels, the small cord half that number.

units.zh: 白玉雙佩、革帶、玉鉤㫤。
units.en: White jade double pendant, leather belt, and jade belt hook.
units.literal: White jade double pendant, leather belt, and jade belt hook.

units.zh: 冕制。
units.en: Specifications for the Crown
units.literal: Regulations for the crown.

units.zh: 天板長一尺六寸，廣八寸，前高八寸五分，後高九寸五分，身圍一尺八寸三分，並納言，並用青羅為表，紅羅為裏，周回用金棱。
units.en: The heaven board measured one chi six cun long and eight cun wide, eight cun five fen high in front and nine cun five fen behind, with a body circumference of one chi eight cun three fen, including the speech-flap; green brocade outside, red within, gilt edges all around.
units.literal: The heaven board was one chi six cun long, eight cun wide, eight cun five fen high in front and nine cun five fen high behind; the body circumference one chi eight cun three fen; all with speech-flap; green brocade outside and red brocade inside, with gilt edges all around.

units.zh: 天板下有四柱，四面珍珠網結子，花素墜子，前後珠旒共二十四，旒各長一尺二寸。
units.en: Four pillars below the heaven board bore pearl nets on all sides with plain pendants; twenty-four pearl tassels front and rear, each one chi two cun long.
units.literal: Below the heaven board were four pillars; pearl nets knotted on all four sides with plain pendants; front and rear pearl tassels totaling twenty-four, each tassel one chi two cun long.

units.zh: 青碧線織造天河帶一，長一丈二尺，闊二寸，兩頭各有真珠金碧旒三節，玉滴子節花。
units.en: A Milky Way band woven in green jade thread, one zhang two chi by two cun, with three sections of pearl and gilt jade-green tassels and jade drip beads at each end.
units.literal: One Milky Way band woven of green jade thread, one zhang two chi long and two cun wide; at both ends three sections of genuine pearl and gilt jade-green tassels with jade drip beads and floral nodes.

units.zh: 紅線組帶二，上有真珠金翠旒，玉滴子節花，下有金鐸子二。
units.en: Two red assembly bands bore pearl and gold-jade tassels with jade drip beads and two gilt bell pendants below.
units.literal: Two red cord assembly bands with genuine pearl and gold-jade tassels, jade drip-bead floral nodes, and two gilt bell pendants below.

units.zh: 梅紅線款幔帶一。
units.en: One plum-red cord patterned hanging band.
units.literal: One plum-red cord patterned hanging band.

units.zh: 黈纊二，真珠垂系，上用金萼子二。
units.en: Two yellow ramie ear fillers with pearl hanging cords and two gilt calyx mounts above.
units.literal: Two yellow ramie ear fillers with pearl hanging cords and two gilt calyx mounts above.

units.zh: 簪窠，款幔、組帶鈿窠，各二，內組帶鈿窠四並玉鏤塵碾造。
units.en: Hairpin sockets and rosettes for patterned hanging and assembly bands, two each; four inner assembly rosettes, all of jade openwork dust-grind work.
units.literal: Hairpin sockets, patterned hanging and assembly band rosettes, two each; inner assembly band rosettes four, all jade openwork dust-grind manufacture.

units.zh: 玉簪一，頂方二寸，導長一尺二寸，簪頂刻鏤塵雲龍。
units.en: One jade hairpin with a two-cun square top, a one-chi-two-cun guide, and openwork dust-cloud dragons carved on the crown.
units.literal: One jade hairpin, top two cun square, guide one chi two cun long, hairpin top carved openwork dust-cloud dragons.

units.zh: 袞，用青羅夾制，五彩間金繪畫，正面日一、月一、升龍四、山十二，上下襟華蟲、火各六對，虎、蜼各六對。
units.en: The robe was lined green brocade with polychrome gold painting: front with one sun, one moon, four ascending dragons, and twelve mountains; upper and lower flaps with six pairs each of floral creatures and fire, and six pairs each of tigers and fu-beasts.
units.literal: Robe: green brocade lined, polychrome gold-painted; on the front one sun, one moon, four ascending dragons, twelve mountains; on upper and lower flaps six pairs each of floral creatures and fire; six pairs each of tigers and fu-beasts.

units.zh: 背面星一，升龍四、山十二，華蟲、火各二十對，虎、蜼各六對。
units.en: The back bore one star, four ascending dragons, twelve mountains, twenty pairs each of floral creatures and fire, and six pairs each of tigers and fu-beasts.
units.literal: On the back one star, four ascending dragons, twelve mountains, twenty pairs each of floral creatures and fire, six pairs each of tigers and fu-beasts.

units.zh: 中單一，白羅單制，羅領、褾、襈。
units.en: One inner garment of single-layer white gauze with gauze collar, border, and lapel.
units.literal: One inner garment, white gauze single-layer, gauze collar, border, and lapel.

units.zh: 裳一，帶、褾襈，紅羅八幅夾制，繡藻三十二，粉十六、米十六、黼三十二、黻三十二。
units.en: One skirt with belt, border, and lapel: eight-panel lined red brocade embroidered with thirty-two algae, sixteen powder-grain, sixteen rice-grain, thirty-two fu, and thirty-two fu-corner motifs.
units.literal: One skirt with belt, border, and lapel; red brocade in eight panels lined, embroidered thirty-two algae, sixteen powder-grain, sixteen rice-grain, thirty-two fu, and thirty-two fu-corner patterns.

units.zh: 蔽膝一，帶、褾、襈，並紅羅夾制，繡升龍二。
units.en: One knee cover with belt, border, and lapel in lined red brocade embroidered with two ascending dragons.
units.literal: One knee cover with belt, border, and lapel, all red brocade lined, embroidered with two ascending dragons.

units.zh: 綬一副：大綬以赤黃黑白綠縹六彩織，紅羅托裏，小綬三色，同大綬，銷金黃羅綬頭，上間施三玉環，皆刻雲龍，大綬五百首，小綬半之。
units.en: One cord set: a great six-color cord of scarlet, yellow, black, white, green, and light blue with red brocade backing; a three-color small cord matching it; gold-cut yellow brocade head with three cloud-dragon jade rings; five hundred great-cord tassels and half as many on the small cord.
units.literal: One cord set: great cord woven in six colors of scarlet, yellow, black, white, green, and light blue, red brocade backing; small cord three colors matching the great cord; gold-cut yellow brocade cord head with three jade rings set between, all carved cloud-dragons; great cord five hundred tassels, small cord half.

units.zh: 緋白大帶一，銷金黃羅帶頭，鈿窠二十四。
units.en: One scarlet-white great belt with gold-cut yellow brocade head and twenty-four rosettes.
units.literal: One scarlet-white great belt with gold-cut yellow brocade head and twenty-four rosettes.

units.zh: 紅羅勒帛一，青羅抹帶一。
units.en: One red brocade waist band and one green brocade sash.
units.literal: One red brocade waist band and one green brocade sash.

units.zh: 玉佩二，白玉上中下璜各一，半月各二，皆刻雲龍，玉滴子各二，皆以紅真珠穿制。
units.en: Two jade pendants, each with upper, middle, and lower white jade huang plaques and two half-moons, all carved with cloud-dragons and two jade drip beads, strung on red genuine pearls.
units.literal: Two jade pendants, each with upper, middle, and lower white jade huang plaques one each and two half-moons each, all carved cloud-dragons, two jade drip beads each, all strung on red genuine pearls.

units.zh: 金篦鉤、獸面、水葉、環、釘。
units.en: Gilt comb hooks, beast faces, water leaves, rings, and nails.
units.literal: Gilt comb hooks, beast faces, water leaves, rings, and nails.

units.zh: 涼帶一，紅羅裹，縷金，上有玉鵝七，䤩尾束各一，金攀龍口，以玳瑁板襯釘腳。
units.en: One cool belt wrapped in red brocade with gold thread, seven jade geese above, tin tail bindings, gilt climbing-dragon mouth, and tortoiseshell backing plates for the nail feet.
units.literal: One cool belt, red brocade wrapped, gold thread, with seven jade geese above, one tin tail binding each, gilt climbing-dragon mouth, tortoiseshell plates backing nail feet.

units.zh: 褵，重底、紅羅面，白綾托裏，如意頭，銷金黃羅緣口，玉鼻仁飾以珠。
units.en: Shoes with double soles, red brocade uppers, white damask lining, ruyi toes, gold-cut yellow brocade mouth edges, and pearl-set jade nose ornaments.
units.literal: Shoes: double sole, red brocade upper, white damask lining, ruyi toe, gold-cut yellow brocade mouth edge, jade nose ornament set with pearls.

units.zh: 襪用緋羅加綿。
units.en: Socks were scarlet gauze with cotton padding.
units.literal: Socks used scarlet gauze with cotton padding.

units.zh: 凡大祭祀、加尊號、受冊寶，則服袞冕。
units.en: The robe and crown were worn for great sacrifices, investiture with honorific titles, and reception of registers and seals.
units.literal: For great sacrifices, adding honorific titles, or receiving registers and seals, the robe and crown were worn.

units.zh: 行幸、齋戒出宮或禦正殿，則通天冠、絳紗袍。
units.en: For imperial progresses, fast-day departures from the palace, or audiences in the main hall, the penetration-heaven cap and scarlet gauze robe.
units.literal: For imperial progresses, fast abstention when leaving the palace, or presiding at the main hall, the penetration-heaven cap and scarlet gauze robe.

units.zh: 鎮圭，大圭。
units.en: Stabilizing Jade Tablet; Great Jade Tablet
units.literal: Stabilizing jade tablet; great jade tablet.

units.zh: 皇統九年十月二十四日，禮部下太常，畫鎮圭式樣，大禮使據《三禮圖》以進，用之。
units.en: On the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month, ninth year of Huangtong [1149], the Directorate ordered the Office of Imperial Sacrifices to draft the stabilizing-tablet pattern; the Grand Ritual Commissioner submitted it per the Illustrations of the Three Rites, and it was adopted.
units.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Huangtong, the Directorate of Ceremonial sent down to the Office of Imperial Sacrifices to draw the stabilizing-tablet pattern; the Grand Ritual Commissioner submitted it according to the Illustrations of the Three Rites, and it was used.

units.zh: 大定十一年，太常寺按《禮》「大圭長三尺，抒上終葵首，天子服之」。
units.en: In the eleventh year of Dading [1171], the Office cited the Rites: 'The great tablet is three chi long, narrow above with zhongkui head; the Son of Heaven wears it.'
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading the Office of Imperial Sacrifices cited the Rites: 'The great tablet is three chi long, narrow above with zhongkui head; the Son of Heaven wears it.'

units.zh: 自西魏、隋、唐以來，大圭長尺二寸，與鎮圭同。
units.en: From Western Wei through Sui and Tang, the great tablet was one chi two cun—the same length as the stabilizing tablet.
units.literal: From Western Wei, Sui, and Tang onward, the great tablet was one chi two cun long, the same as the stabilizing tablet.

units.zh: 蓋鎮圭以鎮天下，以四鎮山為飾，今其圭已依古制，惟無大圭。
units.en: The stabilizing tablet symbolized stabilizing the realm and was ornamented with the four stabilizing mountains; that tablet already followed antiquity, but no great tablet existed.
units.literal: The stabilizing tablet stabilizes the realm, ornamented with the four stabilizing mountains; now its tablet already follows antiquity, but there is no great tablet.

units.zh: 今禦府有故宋白玉圭，圓，無上閷及終葵首。
units.en: The imperial storehouse held an old Song white jade tablet, round, without upper narrowing or zhongkui head.
units.literal: Now in the imperial storehouse is an old Song white jade tablet, round, without the upper narrowing or zhongkui head.

units.zh: 自西魏以來，所制玉笏皆長尺有二寸，方而不折，雖非先王之法，蓋後世玉難得，隨宜故也。
units.en: From Western Wei onward, jade tablets were made one chi two cun long and square without bend; though not the ancient standard, later ages adapted because fine jade was scarce.
units.literal: From Western Wei onward, jade tablets made were all one chi two cun long, square without bend; though not the former kings' law, in later ages jade was hard to obtain and they adapted accordingly.

units.zh: 擬合以禦府所藏，行禮就用。
units.en: Officials proposed using the storehouse piece when the rite was performed.
units.literal: It was proposed to use what the imperial storehouse held for ritual when performed.

units.zh: 視朝之服
units.en: Dress for Attending Court
units.literal: Dress for attending court

units.zh: 初，太宗即位，始服赭黃，自後視百官朝禦袍帶。
units.en: When Emperor Taizong first took the throne, he adopted ochre-yellow and thereafter received officials in court robe and belt.
units.literal: At first, when Emperor Taizong took the throne, he first wore ochre-yellow; thereafter he viewed the hundred officials in court robe and belt.

units.zh: 章宗即位，以世宗之喪，有司請禦純吉，不從，乃服淡黃袍、烏犀帶。
units.en: At Emperor Zhangzong's accession, during mourning for Emperor Shizong, officials requested pure auspicious dress; he refused and wore a pale yellow robe with rhinoceros belt.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, because of Emperor Shizong's mourning, offices requested pure auspicious dress; he did not consent, and wore pale yellow robe and rhinoceros belt.

units.zh: 常朝則服小帽、紅襴、偏帶或束帶。
units.en: For routine audiences he wore a small cap, red lan robe, and side belt or bound belt.
units.literal: For regular audiences he wore small cap, red lan robe, and side belt or bound belt.

units.zh: 皇后冠服
units.en: Empress Crown and Dress
units.literal: Empress crown and dress

units.zh: 花株冠，用盛子一，青羅表、青絹襯金紅羅托裏，用九龍、四鳳，前面大龍銜穗球一朵，前後有花株各十有二，及鸂鶒、孔雀、雲鶴、王母仙人隊、浮動插瓣等，後有納言，上有金蟬鑻金兩博鬢，以上並用鋪翠滴粉縷金裝珍珠結制，下有金圈口，上用七鈿窠，後有金鈿窠二，穿紅羅鋪金款幔帶一。
units.en: Flower-cluster crown: one shengzi base with green brocade and silk lining on gold-red brocade, bearing nine dragons and four phoenixes; a front great dragon holding a tassel ball; twelve flower clusters front and rear, with mandarin ducks, peacocks, cloud cranes, Queen Mother processions, and floating petals; speech-flap behind; gilt cicada and double temple locks with kingfisher, powdered gold, and pearls; gilt rim with seven rosettes above and two behind, threaded through a red brocade spread-gold patterned hanging band.
units.literal: Flower-cluster crown: one shengzi base, green brocade outside and green silk lining with gold-red brocade backing, using nine dragons and four phoenixes; a large dragon in front holding a tassel ball; front and rear twelve flower clusters each, with mandarin ducks, peacocks, cloud cranes, Queen Mother immortal processions, floating inserted petals, and the like; speech-flap behind; above, gilt cicada and gilt double temple-side locks, all with spread kingfisher, powdered gold thread, and pearl knots; below a gilt rim with seven rosettes above and two gilt rosettes behind, passing through one red brocade spread-gold patterned hanging band.

units.zh: 禕衣，深青羅織成翬翟之形，素質，十二等，領、褾、襈並紅羅織成雲龍，中單以素青紗制，領織成黼形霰十二，褾、袖襈、織成雲龍，並織紅縠造。
units.en: Yi robe: deep green brocade woven with pheasant forms on a plain twelve-grade body; collar, border, and lapel in red brocade cloud-dragons; inner garment of plain green gauze with collar hail patterns in fu form, borders and sleeves in red damask cloud-dragons.
units.literal: Yi robe: deep green brocade woven into pheasant forms, plain body, twelve grades; collar, border, and lapel all red brocade woven cloud-dragons; inner garment of plain green gauze, collar woven twelve fu-form hail patterns, border, sleeve lapel, and woven cloud-dragons all red damask weave.

units.zh: 裳，八副，深青羅織成翟文六等，褾、襈織成紅羅雲龍，明金帶腰。
units.en: Skirt of eight panels in deep green brocade with six-grade pheasant patterns; borders and lapels in red brocade cloud-dragons; bright-gold waist belt.
units.literal: Skirt, eight panels, deep green brocade woven pheasant patterns in six grades; border and lapel red brocade cloud-dragons; bright-gold belt at waist.

units.zh: 蔽膝，深青羅織成翟文三等，領緣，緅色羅織成雲龍，明金帶大綬一，長五尺，闊一尺，黃赤白黑縹綠六彩織成，小綬三色同大綬，間七寶鈿窠，施三玉環。
units.en: Knee cover in three-grade deep green brocade pheasant patterns with russet cloud-dragon collar edge; bright-gold great cord five chi by one chi in six colors; matching three-color small cord with seven-treasure rosettes and three jade rings.
units.literal: Knee cover: deep green brocade woven pheasant patterns in three grades, collar edge in russet brocade cloud-dragons; one bright-gold great cord five chi long and one chi wide, woven in six colors of yellow, scarlet, white, black, light blue, and green; small cord three colors matching great cord, with seven-treasure rosettes between and three jade rings set.

units.zh: 上碾雲龍，拈金線織成大小綬頭，紅羅花襯，大帶，青羅硃裏，紕其外，上以硃錦，下以綠錦，紐約用青組，拈金線織成帶頭。
units.en: Cloud-dragons ground above; gold-thread woven cord heads; red brocade floral lining; great belt of green brocade with vermilion lining, vermilion brocade above and green below, green cord fasteners with gold-thread woven heads.
units.literal: Above ground cloud-dragons; twisted gold thread woven large and small cord heads; red brocade floral lining; great belt green brocade vermilion lining, piping outside, vermilion brocade above and green brocade below, fasteners green cord, cord head twisted gold thread weave.

units.zh: 玉佩二朵，每朵上中下璜各一，半月墜子各二，並玉碾，縷金打鈒獸面、篦鉤佩子各一，水葉子真珠穿綴。
units.en: Two jade pendants, each with upper, middle, and lower huang and two half-moons, jade-ground with gold-thread beast faces, comb hooks, and pearl-strung water leaves.
units.literal: Two jade pendants, each with upper, middle, and lower huang one each and two half-moon pendants each, all jade ground; gold-thread chased beast face, comb hook pendants one each, water leaves strung with genuine pearls.

units.zh: 青衣革帶，用縷金青羅裹造，上用金打鈒水地龍，鵝眼䤩尾，龍口攀束子共八事，以玳瑁襯金釘腳。
units.en: Green leather belt wrapped in gold-thread green brocade with chased water-ground dragons, goose-eye tin tails, dragon-mouth bindings—eight items—with tortoiseshell-backed gilt nail feet.
units.literal: Green garment leather belt, gold-thread green brocade wrap, above with gold chased water-ground dragons, eight items including goose-eye tin tail and dragon-mouth climbing bindings, tortoiseshell backing gilt nail feet.

units.zh: 抹帶二，紅羅、青羅各一，並明金造，各長一丈五寸。
units.en: Two sashes, red and green brocade, bright-gold work, each one zhang five cun long.
units.literal: Two sashes, one red brocade and one green brocade, both bright-gold manufacture, each one zhang five cun long.

units.zh: 褵以青羅制，白綾裏，如意頭，明金、黃羅准上用，玉鼻仁真珠裝，綴系帶。
units.en: Shoes of green brocade with white damask lining, ruyi toes, bright gold and yellow brocade trim, pearl-set jade nose ornaments, and fastening bands.
units.literal: Shoes made of green brocade, white damask lining, ruyi toe, bright gold and yellow brocade for superior use, jade nose ornament with genuine pearls, attached fastening bands.

units.zh: 襪，青羅表裏，綴系帶。
units.en: Socks of green brocade inside and out with fastening bands.
units.literal: Socks, green brocade outside and inside, attached fastening bands.

units.zh: 犀冠，減撥花樣，縷金裝造，上有玉簪一，下有玳瑁盤一。
units.en: Rhinoceros crown with reduced spread-flower pattern in gold thread, jade hairpin above and tortoiseshell disk below.
units.literal: Rhinoceros crown, reduced spread-flower pattern, gold-thread manufacture, one jade hairpin above, one tortoiseshell disk below.

units.zh: 皇太子冠服
units.en: Crown Prince Crown and Dress
units.literal: Crown prince crown and dress

units.zh: 冕用白珠九旒，紅絲組為纓，青纊充耳，犀簪導。
units.en: The crown bore nine white-pearl tassels, red silk chin straps, green ramie ear fillers, and a rhinoceros hairpin guide.
units.literal: Crown used white pearls for nine tassels, red silk cords for the chin strap, green ramie ear fillers, rhinoceros hairpin guide.

units.zh: 袞，青衣硃裳，五章在衣，山、龍、華蟲、火、宗彝，四章在裳，藻、粉米、黼、黻。
units.en: Robe of green upper garment and vermilion skirt: five emblems on the garment (mountains, dragons, floral creatures, fire, ancestral vessels) and four on the skirt (algae, powder-grain, fu, fu-corner).
units.literal: Robe: green upper garment and vermilion skirt; five emblems on the garment—mountains, dragons, floral creatures, fire, and ancestral vessels; four on the skirt—algae, powder-grain, fu, and fu-corner.

units.zh: 白紗中單，青褾襈裾。
units.en: White gauze inner garment with green border, lapel, and hem.
units.literal: White gauze inner garment, green border, lapel, and hem.

units.zh: 革帶，塗金銀鉤㫤。
units.en: Leather belt with gilt silver hook.
units.literal: Leather belt with gilt silver hook.

units.zh: 蔽膝，隨裳色，為火、山二章。
units.en: Knee cover matching the skirt, bearing fire and mountain emblems.
units.literal: Knee cover following skirt color, with fire and mountain two emblems.

units.zh: 瑜玉雙佩，四采織成大綬，間施玉環三。
units.en: Fine jade double pendant and great four-color cord with three jade rings between.
units.literal: Fine jade double pendant, great cord woven in four colors with three jade rings set between.

units.zh: 白襪，硃褵，褵加金塗銀釦。
units.en: White socks and vermilion shoes with added gilt silver clasps.
units.literal: White socks, vermilion shoes; shoes with gilt silver clasps added.

units.zh: 謁廟則服之。
units.en: Worn when visiting temples.
units.literal: Worn when visiting temples.

units.zh: 遠遊冠，十八梁，金塗銀花，飾博山附蟬，紅絲組為纓，犀簪導。
units.en: Far-travel cap of eighteen beams with gilt silver flowers, Mount Bo and cicada ornaments, red silk chin strap, and rhinoceros guide.
units.literal: Far-travel cap, eighteen beams, gilt silver flowers, ornamented with Mount Bo and attached cicada, red silk cords for chin strap, rhinoceros hairpin guide.

units.zh: 硃明服，紅裳，白紗中單，方心曲領。
units.en: Vermilion-bright dress: scarlet skirt, white gauze inner garment, square-heart curved collar.
units.literal: Vermilion-bright dress: scarlet skirt, white gauze inner garment, square-heart curved collar.

units.zh: 絳紗蔽膝，白襪黑褵。
units.en: Scarlet gauze knee cover with white socks and black shoes.
units.literal: Scarlet gauze knee cover, white socks and black shoes.

units.zh: 餘同袞冕。
units.en: All else matched the robe and crown.
units.literal: The rest as the robe and crown.

units.zh: 冊寶則服之。
units.en: Worn for registers and seals.
units.literal: Worn for registers and seals.

units.zh: 桓圭，長九寸、廣三寸、厚半寸、用白玉，若屋之桓楹，為二棱。
units.en: Pillar tablet of white jade, nine cun long, three cun wide, half a cun thick, ridged like a hall pillar.
units.literal: Pillar tablet, nine cun long, three cun wide, half a cun thick, white jade; like a hall pillar, made with two ridges.

units.zh: 太子入朝起居及與宴，則朝服，紫袍、玉帶、雙魚袋。
units.en: For court attendance and banquets the crown prince wore court dress: purple robe, jade belt, and double-fish pouch.
units.literal: When the crown prince entered court for attendance and banquets, he wore court dress: purple robe, jade belt, and double-fish pouch.

units.zh: 其視事及見師少賓客，則服小帽、皁衫、玉束帶。
units.en: For official business or receiving teachers and junior guests, he wore a small cap, black robe, and jade bound belt.
units.literal: When conducting affairs or receiving teachers and junior guests, he wore small cap, black robe, and jade bound belt.

units.zh: 宗室及外戚並一品命婦
units.en: Imperial Clan, Maternal Kin, and First-Rank Titled Ladies
units.literal: Imperial clan, maternal kin, and first-rank titled ladies

units.zh: 衣服聽用明金，期親雖別籍、女子出嫁並同。
units.en: They might use bright gold on clothing; close kin remained eligible even if registered separately or if daughters had married out.
units.literal: Clothing was permitted bright gold; close kin even if registered separately, and daughters who had married out, were the same.

units.zh: 又五品以上官母、妻，許披霞帔。
units.en: Mothers and wives of officials fifth rank and above might also wear cloud-collar capes.
units.literal: Moreover, mothers and wives of officials fifth rank and above were permitted to wear cloud-collar capes.

units.zh: 唯首飾、霞帔、領袖、腰帶，許用明金、籠金、間金之類。
units.en: Bright gold, caged gold, and mixed gold were permitted only on head ornaments, cloud-collar capes, collars, sleeves, and waist belts.
units.literal: Only for head ornaments, cloud-collar capes, collar and sleeves, and waist belts were bright gold, caged gold, and mixed gold types permitted.

units.zh: 其衣服止用明銀、象金及金條壓繡。
units.en: On clothing itself only bright silver, imitation gold, and gold-thread pressed embroidery were allowed.
units.literal: For clothing only bright silver, imitation gold, and gold-thread pressed embroidery were used.

units.zh: 正班局分承應帶官人，雖未出職系班，其祖母及母、妻、子孫之婦、同籍兄弟之妻、及在室女、孫、姊妹並同。
units.en: The same applied to grandmothers, mothers, wives, sons' wives, brothers' wives under the same register, unmarried daughters, granddaughters, and sisters of regular-rank bureau attendants with official belts, even before substantive appointment.
units.literal: Regular-rank bureau attendants with official belts, though not yet holding substantive posts in the roster, their grandmothers and mothers, wives, sons' wives, same-register brothers' wives, unmarried daughters, granddaughters, and sisters were the same.

units.zh: 又禁私家用純黃帳幕陳設，若曾經宣賜鸞輿服禦，日月雲肩、龍文黃服、五個鞘眼之鞍皆須更改。
units.en: Private households were forbidden pure yellow curtains and furnishings; any imperial bestowal of luan-carriage dress, sun-moon cloud-shoulder robes, dragon yellow dress, or five-sheath-eye saddles had to be altered.
units.literal: It was also forbidden for private households to use pure yellow curtains and furnishings; if ever bestowed imperial luan-carriage dress, sun-moon cloud-shoulder, dragon-pattern yellow dress, or saddles with five sheath eyes, all had to be altered.

units.zh: 臣下朝服
units.en: Ministers' Court Dress
units.literal: Ministers' court dress

units.zh: 凡導駕及行大禮，文武百官皆服之。
units.en: All civil and military officials wore it when guiding the imperial carriage or performing great ceremonies.
units.literal: Whenever guiding the imperial carriage or performing great ceremonies, civil and military officials of all ranks wore it.

units.zh: 正一品：貂蟬籠巾，七梁額花冠，貂鼠立筆，銀立筆，犀簪導，佩劍，緋羅大袖、緋羅裙、緋羅蔽膝各一，緋白羅大帶，天下樂暈錦玉環綬一，白羅方心曲領、白紗中單、銀褐勒帛各一，玉珠佩二，金塗銀革帶，烏皮履，白綾襪。
units.en: Positive first rank: sable-tail caged headwrap, seven-beam forehead-flower crown, sable and silver upright brushes, rhinoceros guide, sword, scarlet gauze great sleeve, skirt, and knee cover, scarlet-white great belt, All-under-Heaven-Rejoices halo brocade jade-ring cord, white square-heart collar and inner garment, silver-brown waist band, two jade-bead pendants, gilt silver leather belt, black shoes, white damask socks.
units.literal: First rank, positive: sable-tail caged headwrap, seven-beam forehead-flower crown, sable upright brush, silver upright brush, rhinoceros hairpin guide, sword worn, scarlet gauze great sleeve, scarlet gauze skirt, scarlet gauze knee cover one each, scarlet-white gauze great belt, one All-under-Heaven-Rejoices halo brocade jade-ring cord, white gauze square-heart curved collar, white gauze inner garment, silver-brown waist band one each, two jade-bead pendants, gilt silver leather belt, black leather shoes, white damask socks.

units.zh: 正二品：七梁冠，銀立筆，犀簪導，不佩劍，緋羅大袖，雜花暈錦玉環綬，餘並同。
units.en: Positive second rank: seven-beam crown, silver upright brush, rhinoceros guide, no sword, scarlet great sleeve, mixed-flower halo brocade jade-ring cord; otherwise as first rank.
units.literal: Positive second rank: seven-beam crown, silver upright brush, rhinoceros hairpin guide, no sword worn, scarlet gauze great sleeve, mixed-flower halo brocade jade-ring cord; the rest the same.

units.zh: 正四品：五梁冠，銀立筆，犀簪，白獅錦銀環綬，珠佩，銀革帶，禦史中丞則獬豸冠、青荷蓮綬，餘並同。
units.en: Positive fourth rank: five-beam crown, silver brush, rhinoceros hairpin, white-lion brocade silver-ring cord, bead pendant, silver belt; the Vice Censor-in-chief wore xiezhi crown and green lotus cord; otherwise the same.
units.literal: Positive fourth rank: five-beam crown, silver upright brush, rhinoceros hairpin, white-lion brocade silver-ring cord, bead pendant, silver leather belt; the Vice Censor-in-chief then wore xiezhi crown and green lotus cord; the rest the same.

units.zh: 正五品：四梁冠，簇四金雕錦銅環綬，銀珠佩，餘並同。
units.en: Positive fifth rank: four-beam crown, four-cluster gold-carved brocade copper-ring cord, silver bead pendant; otherwise the same.
units.literal: Positive fifth rank: four-beam crown, clustered four gold-carved brocade copper-ring cord, silver bead pendant; the rest the same.

units.zh: 正六品至七品：三梁冠，黃獅錦銅環綬，銅珠佩，銅束帶，餘並同。
units.en: Positive sixth through seventh rank: three-beam crown, yellow-lion brocade copper-ring cord, copper bead pendant, copper belt; otherwise the same.
units.literal: Positive sixth through seventh rank: three-beam crown, yellow-lion brocade copper-ring cord, copper bead pendant, copper bound belt; the rest the same.

units.zh: 大定二十二年祫享，攝官、導駕二品冠七梁，三品四品冠六梁，服有金花，五品冠五梁，六品冠四梁，七品冠三梁，監察禦史獬豸冠、青綬，八品九品冠二梁，餘制並同。
units.en: At the joint sacrifice of the twenty-second year of Dading [1182], acting officials wore: guiding second rank seven beams; third and fourth ranks six beams with gold-floral dress; fifth rank five beams; sixth rank four; seventh rank three; investigating censor xiezhi crown and green cord; eighth and ninth ranks two beams; all else unchanged.
units.literal: In the joint sacrifice of the twenty-second year of Dading, acting officials: guiding second rank seven-beam crown, third and fourth ranks six-beam crown with gold-floral dress, fifth rank five-beam crown, sixth rank four-beam crown, seventh rank three-beam crown; investigating censor xiezhi crown and green cord; eighth and ninth ranks two-beam crown; the rest of the regulations the same.

units.zh: 三品舊無。
units.en: Third rank had no separate specification formerly.
units.literal: Third rank formerly had none.

units.zh: 皇統七年，太常寺言：「太廟成後，奉安神主，祫享行禮，凡行事、執事、助祭、陪位官，准古典當服袞冕、九章畫降龍，隨品各有等差。
units.en: In the seventh year of Huangtong [1147], the Office of Imperial Sacrifices reported: 'After the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed and spirit tablets enshrined, officials conducting, assisting, or attending the joint sacrifice should wear robe and crown bearing nine emblems with painted descending dragons, graded by rank per classical precedent.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Huangtong, the Office of Imperial Sacrifices said: 'After the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed, when enshrining spirit tablets and performing the joint sacrifice rites, all officials conducting affairs, holding office, assisting sacrifice, and attending in place should according to classical precedent wear robe and crown with nine emblems painted descending dragons, each rank having its gradation.

units.zh: 《通典》雲虞、夏、殷並十二章，日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲作繪于衣，宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻絺繡於裳。
units.en: The Comprehensive Institutions records that Yu, Xia, and Yin all used twelve emblems: sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, and floral creatures painted on the upper garment; ancestral vessels, algae, fire, powder-grain, fu, and fu-corner fine-embroidered on the skirt.
units.literal: The Comprehensive Institutions states that Yu, Xia, and Yin all had twelve emblems: sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, and floral creatures painted on the garment; ancestral vessels, algae, fire, powder-grain, fu, and fu-corner fine-embroidered on the skirt.

units.zh: 周升三辰於旂，登龍於山，登火于宗彝，作九章之服，龍、山、華蟲、火、宗彝繪於衣，藻、粉米、黼、黻繡於裳。
units.en: Zhou raised the three luminaries to the banner, set dragons on mountains and fire on ancestral vessels, and made nine-emblem dress with dragons, mountains, floral creatures, fire, and ancestral vessels painted on the garment and algae, powder-grain, fu, and fu-corner embroidered on the skirt.
units.literal: Zhou raised the three luminaries to the banner, set dragons on mountains, set fire on ancestral vessels, and made nine-emblem dress: dragons, mountains, floral creatures, fire, and ancestral vessels painted on the garment; algae, powder-grain, fu, and fu-corner embroidered on the skirt.

units.zh: '公之服自袞冕而下如王之服，候伯之服自鷩冕而下如公之服'。
units.en: The duke's dress from robe and crown downward matched the king's; the marquis and earl's from pheasant crown downward matched the duke's.
units.literal: The duke's dress from robe and crown downward was like the king's dress; the marquis and earl's dress from pheasant crown downward was like the duke's dress.

units.zh: 又後魏帝服袞冕，與祭者皆朝服。
units.en: In Later Wei the emperor wore robe and crown, yet all sacrifice participants wore court dress.
units.literal: Moreover, in Later Wei the emperor wore robe and crown, but those participating in sacrifice all wore court dress.

units.zh: 又《開元禮》一品服九章。
units.en: The Kaiyuan Rites likewise assigned nine emblems to first rank.
units.literal: Moreover, the Kaiyuan Rites had first rank wear nine emblems.

units.zh: 又《五禮新儀》正一品服九旒冕、犀簪，青衣畫降龍。
units.en: The New Rituals of the Five Ceremonies specified positive first rank: nine-tassel crown, rhinoceros hairpin, and green garment painted with descending dragons.
units.literal: Moreover, the New Rituals of the Five Ceremonies had positive first rank wear nine-tassel crown and rhinoceros hairpin, green garment painted with descending dragons.

units.zh: 今汴京舊禮直官言，自宣和二年已後，一品祭服七旒冕、大袖無龍。
units.en: Bianjing ritual officers reported that from the second year of Xuanhe [1120] onward, first-rank sacrificial dress used a seven-tassel crown and great sleeves without dragons.
units.literal: Now Bianjing old-ritual direct officials said that from the second year of Xuanhe onward, first-rank sacrificial dress was seven-tassel crown and great sleeve without dragons.

units.zh: 唐雖服九章服，當時司禮少常伯孫茂道言：'諸臣之章雖殊，然飾龍名袞，尊卑相亂，請三公服鷩冕八章為宜。
units.en: Tang officials wore nine emblems, yet Vice Minister of Rites Sun Maodao argued: 'Though ministers' emblems differ, dragon ornament still makes all robes alike and blurs rank; the three dukes should wear pheasant crown with eight emblems.'
units.literal: Though Tang wore nine-emblem dress, at the time Vice Minister of Rites Sun Maodao said: 'Though ministers' emblems differ, yet ornamenting with dragons and calling it robe confuses noble and base; it would be fitting for the three dukes to wear pheasant crown with eight emblems.'

units.zh: '臣等竊謂歷代衣服之制不同，若從後魏則止服朝服，或用宋服則為七章，若遵唐九章，則有飾龍名袞尊卑相亂之議。」
units.en: We note that dress regulations differ by dynasty: Later Wei used only court dress; Song used seven emblems; Tang's nine emblems revived the complaint that dragon ornament and the name robe blur rank.'
units.literal: We humbly consider that clothing regulations differ by dynasty: if following Later Wei one wears only court dress; if using Song dress it is seven emblems; if following Tang's nine emblems, there is the objection that dragon ornament and the name robe confuse noble and base.'

units.zh: 尚書省乃奏用後魏故事，止用燕京大冊禮時所服朝服以祭。
units.en: The Secretariat memorialized to follow Later Wei and use only the court dress worn at Yanjing's great investiture rite for sacrifice.
units.literal: The Secretariat then memorialized using the Later Wei precedent, employing only the court dress worn at the Yanjing great investiture rite for sacrifice.

units.zh: 大定三年八月，詔遵皇統制，攝官則朝服，散官則公服，以皇太子為亞獻，服袞冕。
units.en: In the eighth month of the third year of Dading [1163], an edict followed Huangtong practice: acting officials in court dress, honorary officials in official dress, and the crown prince as secondary offerer in robe and crown.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Dading, an edict ordered following the Huangtong regulations: acting officials wore court dress, honorary officials wore official dress, and the crown prince as secondary offerer wore robe and crown.

units.zh: 十四年，用唐制，若祭遇雨雪則服常服，謂今之公服也。
units.en: In the fourteenth year [1174], Tang practice applied: if rain or snow fell during sacrifice, regular dress—today's official dress—was worn.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year Tang regulations were used: if sacrifice encountered rain or snow, regular dress was worn—meaning today's official dress.

units.zh: 泰和元年八月，禮官言：「祭服所以接神，朝服所以事君，雖歷代損益不同，然未嘗不有分別。
units.en: In the eighth month of the first year of Taihe [1201], ritual officials argued: 'Sacrificial dress receives the spirits and court dress serves the ruler; though dynasties altered the details, the distinction was never abandoned.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Taihe, ritual officials said: 'Sacrificial dress receives the spirits; court dress serves the ruler; though dynasties added and reduced differently, there was never no distinction.

units.zh: 是以袞冕十二旒，玄衣纁裳備十二章，天子之祭服也。
units.en: Thus robe and crown with twelve tassels and black upper garment with scarlet skirt bearing twelve emblems constituted the Son of Heaven's sacrificial dress.
units.literal: Therefore robe and crown with twelve tassels, black upper garment and scarlet skirt completing twelve emblems, was the Son of Heaven's sacrificial dress.

units.zh: 通天冠、絳紗袍、紅羅裳，天子之視朝服也。
units.en: Penetration-heaven cap, scarlet gauze robe, and red brocade skirt were the Son of Heaven's dress for court audiences.
units.literal: Penetration-heaven cap, scarlet gauze robe, and red brocade skirt were the Son of Heaven's court-audience dress.

units.zh: 臣下之服則用青衣硃裳以祭，硃衣硃裳以朝。
units.en: Ministers sacrificed in green upper garment and vermilion skirt and attended court in vermilion upper garment and vermilion skirt.
units.literal: Ministers' dress used green upper garment and vermilion skirt for sacrifice, vermilion upper garment and vermilion skirt for court.

units.zh: 國朝惟天子備袞冕、通天冠二等之服，今群臣但有朝服，而祭服尚闕，每有祀事但以朝服從事，實於典禮未當。
units.en: Only the Son of Heaven possessed both robe-and-crown and penetration-heaven dress; officials had court dress but no sacrificial dress and used court dress at every sacrifice—improper under the canon.
units.literal: Our dynasty alone had the Son of Heaven equipped with robe and crown and penetration-heaven cap as two grades of dress; now the hundred officials had only court dress while sacrificial dress was still lacking; whenever there was a sacrifice they merely used court dress—truly improper to the canon.

units.zh: 請依漢、唐故事，祭服冕旒畫章，然君臣冕服雖章數各殊而俱飾龍名袞，而唐孫茂道已有尊卑相亂之論。
units.en: They proposed Han and Tang sacrificial dress with tasseled crowns and painted emblems, yet minister and ruler alike bore dragons and were called robe—exactly the rank confusion Sun Maodao had criticized in Tang.
units.literal: We request following Han and Tang precedent for sacrificial dress with crown tassels and painted emblems; yet though minister and ruler crown dress differed in emblem count, both ornamented dragons and were called robe, and Tang's Sun Maodao already had the argument that noble and base were confused.

units.zh: 然三公法服有龍，恐涉于僭，國初禮官亦嘗駁議。
units.en: Yet statutory dress for the three dukes included dragons, risking imperial presumption—a point early Jin ritualists had already challenged.
