units.literal: Yet the three dukes' statutory dress had dragons, fearing encroachment on imperial privilege; early Jin ritual officials had also once objected.

units.zh: 乞參酌古今，改置祭服，其冠則如朝冠，而但去其貂蟬、豎筆，其服用青衣、硃裳、白襪、硃履，非攝事者則用朝服，庶幾少有差別。」
units.en: They asked to consult past and present and establish sacrificial dress: court-style crown without sable tail or upright brush; green upper garment, vermilion skirt, white socks, and vermilion shoes; non-acting officials in court dress—so some distinction might remain.'
units.literal: We beg to consult past and present and remake sacrificial dress: the crown like court crown but removing sable tail and upright brush; the dress green upper garment, vermilion skirt, white socks, and vermilion shoes; those not acting in the rite use court dress—thus there may be some distinction.'

units.zh: 上曰：「朝、祭之服，固宜分也。」
units.en: The emperor replied: 'Court dress and sacrificial dress ought indeed to be separate.'
units.literal: The emperor said: 'Court and sacrificial dress ought indeed to be separate.'

units.zh: 大定官制，文資五品以上官服紫。
units.en: Under the Dading official system, civil officials fifth rank and above wore purple.
units.literal: Under the Dading official system, civil officials of fifth rank and above wore purple.

units.zh: 三師、三公、親王、宰相一品官服大獨科花羅，徑不過五寸，執政官服小獨科花羅，徑不過三寸。
units.en: The Three Preceptors, three dukes, princes, and first-rank chief ministers wore large single-stem floral brocade no more than five cun across; chief councillors wore small single-stem floral brocade no more than three cun.
units.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Guardian, three dukes, princes, and first-rank chief ministers wore large single-stem floral brocade, diameter not exceeding five cun; chief councillors wore small single-stem floral brocade, diameter not exceeding three cun.

units.zh: 二品、三品服散搭花羅，謂無枝葉者，徑不過寸半。
units.en: Second and third ranks wore scattered floral brocade without branches or leaves, not exceeding one and a half cun across.
units.literal: Second and third ranks wore scattered floral brocade, meaning without branches and leaves, diameter not exceeding one and a half cun.

units.zh: 四品、五品服小雜花羅，謂花頭碎小者，徑不過一寸。
units.en: Fourth and fifth ranks wore small mixed floral brocade with fine fragmented blossoms, not exceeding one cun across.
units.literal: Fourth and fifth ranks wore small mixed floral brocade, meaning small fragmented floral heads, diameter not exceeding one cun.

units.zh: 六品、七品服緋芝麻羅。
units.en: Sixth and seventh ranks wore scarlet sesame brocade.
units.literal: Sixth and seventh ranks wore scarlet sesame brocade.

units.zh: 八品、九品服綠無紋羅。
units.en: Eighth and ninth ranks wore plain green brocade.
units.literal: Eighth and ninth ranks wore green unpatterned brocade.

units.zh: 應武官皆服紫。
units.en: All military officials wore purple.
units.literal: All military officials wore purple.

units.zh: 凡散官、職事皆從一高，上得兼下，下不得僭上，窄紫亦同服色，各依官制品格。
units.en: Honorary and substantive offices followed whichever rank was higher; superiors might combine downward but inferiors might not usurp upward; narrow purple followed the same color rules by grade.
units.literal: For all honorary and substantive offices one followed the higher, the superior could combine with the inferior, the inferior might not usurp the superior; narrow purple followed the same color rule, each according to office grade and specification.

units.zh: 其諸局分承應人並服無紋素羅。
units.en: All bureau attendants wore unpatterned plain gauze.
units.literal: All bureau attendants wore unpatterned plain gauze.

units.zh: 十五年制曰：「袍不加襴，非古也。」
units.en: A fifteenth-year regulation declared: 'Robes without lan borders are uncanonical.'
units.literal: Fifteenth-year regulation said: 'Robe without lan border is not ancient.'

units.zh: 遂命文資官公服皆加襴。
units.en: Civil officials' official dress was then required to add lan borders.
units.literal: Thereupon civil officials' official dress all received lan borders.

units.zh: 帶制，皇太子玉帶，佩玉雙魚袋。
units.en: Belt regulations: the crown prince wore a jade belt with jade double-fish pouch.
units.literal: Belt regulations: crown prince jade belt, wearing jade double-fish pouch.

units.zh: 親王玉帶，佩玉魚。
units.en: Princes wore jade belts with jade fish.
units.literal: Princes jade belt, wearing jade fish.

units.zh: 一品玉帶，佩金魚。
units.en: First rank: jade belt with gold fish.
units.literal: First rank jade belt, wearing gold fish.

units.zh: 二品笏頭球文金帶，佩金魚。
units.en: Second rank: tablet-head ball-pattern gold belt with gold fish.
units.literal: Second rank tablet-head ball-pattern gold belt, wearing gold fish.

units.zh: 三品、四品荔枝或禦仙花金帶，並佩金魚。
units.en: Third and fourth ranks: lychee or imperial immortal-flower gold belt, all with gold fish.
units.literal: Third and fourth ranks lychee or imperial immortal-flower gold belt, all wearing gold fish.

units.zh: 五品，服紫者紅鞓烏犀帶，佩金魚，服緋者紅鞓烏犀帶，佩銀魚，服綠者並皁鞓烏犀帶。
units.en: Fifth rank: purple dress meant red-girdle rhinoceros belt with gold fish; scarlet meant red-girdle rhinoceros belt with silver fish; green meant black-girdle rhinoceros belt.
units.literal: Fifth rank: those wearing purple used red-girdle rhinoceros belt with gold fish; those wearing scarlet used red-girdle rhinoceros belt with silver fish; those wearing green all used black-girdle rhinoceros belt.

units.zh: 武官，一品、二品佩帶同，三品、四品金帶，五品、六品、七品紅鞓烏犀帶，皆不佩魚，八品以下並皁鞓烏犀帶。
units.en: Military officials: first and second ranks shared belt rules; third and fourth ranks gold belt; fifth through seventh red-girdle rhinoceros belt without fish; eighth rank and below black-girdle rhinoceros belt.
units.literal: Military officials: first and second rank belts the same; third and fourth rank gold belt; fifth, sixth, and seventh rank red-girdle rhinoceros belt, none wearing fish; eighth rank and below all black-girdle rhinoceros belt.

units.zh: 司天、太醫、內侍、教坊，服皆同文武官，惟不佩魚。
units.en: Astronomers, imperial physicians, inner attendants, and Music Bureau officials dressed like civil and military officers but wore no fish.
units.literal: Directorate of Astronomy, Imperial Physicians, inner attendants, and Music Bureau: dress all as civil and military officials, only not wearing fish.

units.zh: 應殿庭承應五品以下官，非入內不許金帶，又展紫入殿庭者，並許服紅鞓，不佩魚。
units.en: Hall attendants fifth rank and below might not use gold belts unless entering the inner palace; those spreading purple in the hall court might use red girdles without fish.
units.literal: Hall-attendant officials fifth rank and below, unless entering the inner palace were not permitted gold belts; those spreading purple in the hall court were all permitted red girdles without fish.

units.zh: 又二品以上官，許兼服通犀帶，三品官若治事及見賓客，許兼服花犀帶。
units.en: Officials second rank and above might also wear penetrating rhinoceros belts; third-rank officials conducting business or receiving guests might wear floral rhinoceros belts.
units.literal: Moreover, officials second rank and above were permitted also to wear penetrating rhinoceros belt; third-rank officials when conducting affairs or receiving guests were permitted also to wear floral rhinoceros belt.

units.zh: 大定二年制，百官趨朝、赴省，並須裹帶。
units.en: A Dading second-year rule required all officials to wear wrapped belts when hurrying to court or attending their ministry.
units.literal: Second-year-of-Dading regulation: all officials hurrying to court or going to their ministry all had to wrap the belt.

units.zh: 五品以上官，趨朝則朝服，赴省則展皁，雨雪沾衣則從便。
units.en: Fifth rank and above wore court dress when hurrying to audience and spread black at the ministry; rain or snow permitted convenience.
units.literal: Officials fifth rank and above: hurrying to court then court dress, going to the ministry then spread black; if rain or snow stained clothing they followed convenience.

units.zh: 凡朝參，主寶、主符展紫，禦仙花或太平花金束帶。
units.en: At court attendance, seal and talisman keepers spread purple with imperial immortal-flower or great-peace-flower gold bound belts.
units.literal: For all court attendance, keepers of seals and talismans spread purple, imperial immortal-flower or great-peace-flower gold bound belt.

units.zh: 近侍給使、供御筆硯、直長、符寶吏紫襖子，塗金束帶。
units.en: Close attendants, imperial writing supply clerks, duty chiefs, and talisman clerks wore purple jackets with gilt bound belts.
units.literal: Close attendants, supply clerks for imperial brush and inkstone, duty chiefs, and talisman clerks wore purple jackets and gilt bound belts.

units.zh: 輪直，則近侍給使並常服，常服則展紫。
units.en: On rotation duty, close attendants and supply clerks wore regular dress—spreading purple.
units.literal: On rotation duty, close attendants and supply clerks all wore regular dress; regular dress meant spreading purple.

units.zh: 閣門六尚，遇朝參侍立則服本品服，若宮中當直則服窄紫、金帶。
units.en: Gate Department chamber officers wore their rank's dress at court but narrow purple and gold belt on palace duty.
units.literal: The six chamber offices of the Gate Department: when attending court and standing in attendance they wore their rank's dress; if on palace duty they wore narrow purple and gold belt.

units.zh: 學士院官、修起居注、補闕、拾遺、秘書丞、秘書郎，朝參侍立則服本品服、色帶。
units.en: Hanlin Academy officials, compilers of the Veritable Record, remonstrance officials, secretaries, and secretarial clerks: when attending court and standing in attendance they wore their rank's dress and colored belt.
units.literal: Hanlin Academy officials, compilers of the Veritable Record, remonstrance officials, secretaries, and secretarial clerks: when attending court and standing in attendance they wore their rank's dress and colored belt.

units.zh: 當直則窄紫、金帶。
units.en: On duty they wore narrow purple and gold belt.
units.literal: On duty then narrow purple and gold belt.

units.zh: 東宮左右衛率、僕正、副僕正、典儀、贊儀、內直郎丞，當直亦許服之。
units.en: Eastern Palace guard commanders, stewards, ritual and praise masters, and inner-duty clerks might wear the same on duty.
units.literal: Eastern Palace left and right guard commanders, chief stewards, deputy chief stewards, ritual masters, praise masters, and inner-duty clerks—on duty they were also permitted to wear them.

units.zh: 太子太師出入宮中則展紫，至東宮則展皁，三少則展紫。
units.en: The crown prince's Grand Preceptor spread purple in the palace and black at the Eastern Palace; the three lesser tutors spread purple.
units.literal: The crown prince's Grand Preceptor entering and leaving the palace spread purple; arriving at the Eastern Palace spread black; the three lesser tutors spread purple.

units.zh: 輿服下
units.en: Carriages and Clothing, Part Three
units.literal: Carriages and clothing, part three

units.zh: 衣服通制
units.en: General Regulations for Clothing
units.literal: General regulations for clothing

units.zh: 君子之服，以稱德也，故德之備者其文備。
units.en: A gentleman's dress should match his virtue; complete virtue calls for complete ornament.
units.literal: The gentleman's dress matches his virtue; therefore when virtue is complete his ornament is complete.

units.zh: 古者王公及士庶人莫不各有一定之制，而不敢相逾者，蓋風俗之奢儉，法令之齊一，必於是而觀焉。
units.en: In antiquity, from kings and dukes to commoners, each rank had fixed dress and dared not overstep—by which one could read custom's extravagance or frugality and law's uniformity.
units.literal: In antiquity kings, dukes, and commoners from scholar to populace each had a fixed regulation and dared not overstep one another—thereby one might observe the extravagance or frugality of custom and the uniformity of law.

units.zh: 《詩》曰：「彼都人士，狐裘黃黃。
units.en: The Odes says: 'Those gentlemen of the capital, in fox fur bright and yellow.
units.literal: The Odes says: 'Those gentlemen of the capital, in fox fur yellow and bright.

units.zh: 其容不改，出言有章。」
units.en: Their bearing unchanged, their speech well ordered.'
units.literal: Their bearing unchanged, their words patterned.'

units.zh: 其三章曰：「彼都人士，充耳琇實。
units.en: The third chapter says: 'Those gentlemen of the capital, ear-stoppers of fine stone.
units.literal: Its third chapter says: 'Those gentlemen of the capital, ear-stoppers of fine stone.

units.zh: 彼君子女，謂之尹吉。」
units.en: Those ladies of the lord, called Yin the auspicious.'
units.literal: Those ladies of the lord, called Yin the auspicious.'

units.zh: 此言都邑之盛，人物之懿也。
units.en: This praises the capital's splendor and its people's excellence.
units.literal: This speaks of the capital's splendor and the people's excellence.

units.zh: 明昌間，章宗謂宰臣曰：「今風俗侈靡，莫若律以制度，使貴賤有等。
units.en: During Mingchang, Emperor Zhangzong told his chief ministers: 'Custom has grown extravagant; we should regulate it by law so rank is clear.
units.literal: In the Mingchang era Emperor Zhangzong told his chief ministers: 'Today custom is extravagant; nothing is better than regulating it by institution so noble and base have grades.

units.zh: 其令禮部具典故以聞。」
units.en: He ordered the Ministry of Rites to gather precedents and report.'
units.literal: Order the Ministry of Rites to gather precedents and report.'

units.zh: 他日又謂參知政事張萬公曰：「山東風俗如何？」
units.en: Another day he asked Vice Director Zhang Wangong: 'How is Shandong custom?'
units.literal: Another day he also said to Vice Director Zhang Wangong: 'How is Shandong custom?'

units.zh: 萬公對以奢，左丞守貞因言衣服之制，上曰：「如卿所言，正恐失人心耳。」
units.en: Wang replied that it was extravagant; Left Vice Director Shouzhen raised clothing regulations; the emperor said: 'As you say, I fear only losing hearts.'
units.literal: Wang answered that it was extravagant; Left Vice Director Shouzhen then spoke on clothing regulations; the emperor said: 'As you say, I fear only losing popular support.'

units.zh: 守貞曰：「止是商賈有不悅者。」
units.en: Shouzhen said: 'Only merchants would be displeased.'
units.literal: Shouzhen said: 'It is only merchants who would be displeased.'

units.zh: 萬公曰：「乞寬與之期，三年之內當如制矣。」
units.en: Wang said: 'Grant a generous deadline; within three years it should match the regulations.'
units.literal: Wang said: 'I beg a generous deadline; within three years it should match the regulations.'

units.zh: 於是，上以禮部所擬太繁，以尚書省所擬而行之。
units.en: The emperor found the Ministry of Rites' draft too elaborate and implemented the Secretariat's version.
units.literal: Thereupon the emperor, because the Ministry of Rites' draft was too elaborate, implemented what the Secretariat drafted.

units.zh: 嗟乎！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 人君以風俗為言，其亦知所務矣。
units.en: When a ruler speaks of custom, he knows what truly matters.
units.literal: When a ruler speaks of custom, he also knows what to attend to.

units.zh: 金人之常服四：帶，巾，盤領衣，烏皮靴。
units.en: Jin regular dress comprised four items: belt, headcloth, round-collar garment, and black leather boots.
units.literal: Jin people's regular dress has four items: belt, headcloth, round-collar garment, and black leather boots.

units.zh: 其束帶曰吐鶻。
units.en: Their bound belt was called tuhe.
units.literal: Their bound belt is called tuhe.

units.zh: 巾之制，以皁羅若紗為之，上結方頂，折垂於後。
units.en: The headcloth was black gauze or silk, tied in a square top above and folded down behind.
units.literal: Headcloth regulation: made of black gauze or gauze, tied in a square top above, folded and hanging behind.

units.zh: 頂之下際兩角各綴方羅徑二寸許，方羅之下各附帶長六七寸。
units.en: Below the top's corners hung square gauze patches about two cun across, each with bands six or seven cun long beneath.
units.literal: Below the junction of the top's two corners square gauze about two cun across was attached; below the square gauze bands about six or seven cun long were attached each.

units.zh: 當橫額之上，或為一縮襞積。
units.en: Above the forehead band there might be one gathered pleat.
units.literal: Above the horizontal forehead, sometimes one gathered pleat fold.

units.zh: 貴顯者于方頂，循十字縫飾以珠，其中必貫以大者，謂之頂珠。
units.en: The eminent ornamented the square top's cross seams with pearls, threading a large one through the center as the top pearl.
units.literal: The eminent on the square top along the cross seam ornamented with pearls; a large one must be threaded through the center, called the top pearl.

units.zh: 帶旁各絡珠結綬，長半帶，垂之，海陵賜大興國者是也。
units.en: Beside the bands hung pearl-knotted cords half the belt's length—the type Prince Hailing bestowed on Daxingguo.
units.literal: Beside the bands pearl knotted cords half the belt length hung down—the kind Prince Hailing bestowed on Daxingguo.

units.zh: 其衣色多白，三品以皁，窄袖，盤領，縫腋，下為襞積，而不缺袴。
units.en: Garments were mostly white; third rank used black: narrow sleeves, round collar, side seams, pleated skirts below, without slit trousers.
units.literal: Garment color was mostly white; third rank used black; narrow sleeves, round collar, side-seam stitching, pleat folds below, and no slit trousers.

units.zh: 其胸臆肩袖，或飾以金繡，其從春水之服則多鶻捕鵝，雜花卉之飾，其從秋山之服則以熊鹿山林為文，其長中骭，取便於騎也。
units.en: Chest, shoulders, and sleeves might bear gold embroidery; spring-water dress favored hawks catching geese and mixed flowers; autumn-mountain dress bore bears, deer, and forests; length reached mid-calf for riding.
units.literal: Chest, shoulders, and sleeves were sometimes ornamented with gold embroidery; spring-water dress mostly had hawk-catching-goose and mixed floral ornament; autumn-mountain dress used bear, deer, and mountain forest patterns; length reaching mid-calf for convenience in riding.

units.zh: 吐鶻，玉為上，金次之，犀象骨角又次之。
units.en: For tuhe belts, jade ranked highest, then gold, then rhinoceros, ivory, bone, and horn.
units.literal: For tuhe, jade was highest, gold next, rhinoceros, ivory, bone, and horn lower still.

units.zh: 銙鞓，小者間置於前，大者施於後，左右有變雙䤩尾，納方束中，其刻琢多如春水秋山之飾。
units.en: Belt plaques: small ones spaced in front, large ones at the rear; paired tin tails left and right fitted into the square binding, carved like spring-water and autumn-mountain motifs.
units.literal: Plaques and girdle: small ones set between in front, large ones at the rear; left and right had paired tin tails; fitted into the square binding; carving mostly like spring-water and autumn-mountain ornament.

units.zh: 左佩牌，右佩刀。
units.en: Plaque on the left, knife on the right.
units.literal: Left wore plaque, right wore knife.

units.zh: 刀貴鑌，柄尚雞舌木，黃黑相半，有黑雙距者為上，或三事五事。
units.en: Knives prized wootz steel with chicken-tongue wood handles half yellow and half black; black double-spur mounts were finest, in three- or five-piece sets.
units.literal: Knives prized wootz steel; handles favored chicken-tongue wood, half yellow half black; those with black double spurs were highest grade, sometimes three-piece or five-piece.

units.zh: 室飾以醬瓣樺，𨭚口飾以鮫，或屑金鍮和漆，塗鮫隙而礲平之。
units.en: Scabbards used sauce-spot birch; mouths ray skin—or gold and brass in lacquer filling ray-skin gaps ground smooth.
units.literal: Scabbard ornamented with sauce-spot birch; mouth ornamented with ray skin; or gold filings and brass mixed with lacquer, ray skin gaps filled and ground smooth.

units.zh: 醬瓣樺者，謂樺皮班文色殷紫如醬中豆瓣也，產其國，故尚之。
units.en: Sauce-spot birch was birch bark mottled dark purple like beans in sauce, native to their land and therefore prized.
units.literal: Sauce-spot birch means birch bark patterned in dark purple like beans in sauce; produced in their country, therefore esteemed.

units.zh: 初，女直人不得改為漢姓及學南人裝束，違者杖八十，編為永制。
units.en: Early on Jurchens might not adopt Han surnames or southern dress; violators received eighty strokes, codified as perpetual law.
units.literal: At first Jurchen people might not change to Han surnames or learn southern dress; violators were beaten eighty strokes and it was compiled as perpetual regulation.

units.zh: 婦人服襜裙，多以黑紫，上編繡全枝花，周身六襞積。
units.en: Women wore dan skirts, mostly black-purple, the upper part woven with full-branch flowers in six pleats all around.
units.literal: Women wore dan skirts, mostly black-purple, upper part woven with full-branch flowers, six pleat folds all around.

units.zh: 上衣謂之團衫，用黑紫或皁及紺，直領，左衽，掖縫，兩傍複為雙襞積，前拂地，後曳地尺餘。
units.en: The upper garment, called a round shirt, was black-purple, black, or dark blue with straight collar and left lapel, side seams, twin pleats on both sides, front brushing the ground and rear trailing over a chi.
units.literal: Upper garment called round shirt, using black-purple or black and dark blue, straight collar, left lapel, side seams, both sides doubled into twin pleats, front brushing the ground, rear trailing more than a chi.

units.zh: 帶色用紅黃，前變垂至下齊。
units.en: Belts were red-yellow with front flaps hanging to the lower hem.
units.literal: Belt color used red-yellow; front flap hanging to lower hem.

units.zh: 年老者以皁紗籠髻如巾狀，散綴玉鈿於上，謂之玉逍遙。
units.en: Elderly women caged their buns in black gauze like a headcloth, scattering jade hairpins above—the jade carefree.
units.literal: The elderly used black gauze to cage the bun like a headcloth, scattering jade hairpins above, called jade carefree.

units.zh: 此皆遼服也，金亦襲之。
units.en: These were Liao styles, which Jin also inherited.
units.literal: These were all Liao dress; Jin also inherited them.

units.zh: 許嫁之女則服綽子，制如婦人服，以紅或銀褐明金為之，對襟彩領，前齊拂地，後曳五寸餘。
units.en: Betrothed daughters wore wrapper coats like women's dress in scarlet or silver-brown bright gold, facing lapels with colored collars, front even with the ground and rear trailing five cun more.
units.literal: A betrothed daughter wore a wrapper coat like women's dress, made of scarlet or silver-brown bright gold, facing lapels with colored collar, front even with the ground, rear trailing five cun more.

units.zh: 明昌六年制，文武官六貫石以上承應人並及廕者，許用牙領，紫圓板皁條羅帶，皁靴，上得兼下。
units.en: Mingchang year six allowed attendants of civil and military officials at six guan-shi and above—and their enfeoffed heirs—ivory collars, purple round-plaque black-stripe gauze belts, and black boots, with downward combination permitted.
units.literal: Mingchang sixth-year regulation: civil and military officials' attendants at six guan-shi and above and their enfeoffed heirs were permitted ivory collars, purple round-plaque black-stripe gauze belt, and black boots; superiors could combine downward.

units.zh: 系籍儒生止服白衫領，系背帶並以紫圓絛羅帶，乾皁靴。
units.en: Registered scholars wore white-shirt collars, back-fastening bands, purple round-cord gauze belts, and dry black boots.
units.literal: Registered scholars wore only white-shirt collars, back-fastening bands, and purple round-cord gauze belts, dry black boots.

units.zh: 餘人用純紫領，不得用緣，雜色圓板絛羅帶不得用紫，靴用黃及黑油皁蠟等，婦人各從便。
units.en: Others used pure purple collars without borders; mixed round-plaque cord belts might not be purple; boots were yellow, black oil, or black wax; women dressed as convenient.
units.literal: Others used pure purple collars without borders; mixed-color round-plaque cord belts might not use purple; boots used yellow and black oil, black wax, and the like; women each followed convenience.

units.zh: 泰和四年，以親王品官既分領緣，而複有皁靴之禁，似涉太煩，遂聽親王用銀褐領紫緣，品官皆紫領白緣，餘從明昌制。
units.en: Taihe year four eased collar rules: princes might use silver-brown collars with purple borders; ranked officials purple collars with white borders; other Mingchang rules remained.
units.literal: Taihe fourth year: because princes and ranked officials already had divided collar borders yet still had black-boot prohibitions, seemingly too tedious, princes were permitted silver-brown collars with purple borders, ranked officials all purple collars with white borders; the rest followed Mingchang regulations.

units.zh: 書袋之制。
units.en: Regulations for Document Pouches
units.literal: Regulations for document pouches.

units.zh: 大定十六年，世宗以吏員與士民之服無別，潛入民間受賕轀獄，有司不能檢察，遂定懸書袋之制。
units.en: In the sixteenth year of Dading [1176], Emperor Shizong found clerks indistinguishable from commoners, secretly taking bribes among the people beyond official inspection, and mandated suspended document pouches.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year of Dading Emperor Shizong, because clerks' dress was indistinguishable from scholars and populace and they secretly entered the populace taking bribes and were thrown into prison while offices could not inspect, the suspended document-pouch regulation was fixed.

units.zh: 省、樞密院令、譯史用紫襜絲為之，台、六部、宗正、統軍司、檢察司以黑斜皮為之，寺、監、隨朝諸局、並州縣，並黃皮為之，各長七寸，闊二寸、厚半寸，並於束帶上懸帶，公退則懸於便服，違者所司糾之。
units.en: Provincial offices, Privy Council orders, and translators used purple dan silk pouches; the Censorate, Six Ministries, Imperial Clan Court, Commandery Office, and Inspection Office used black slanted leather; temples, directorates, court bureaus, and local governments used yellow leather. Each pouch was seven cun long, two cun wide, and half a cun thick, suspended from the official belt and moved to informal dress after hours; violators were disciplined by the responsible office.
units.literal: For provincial offices, Privy Council orders, and translators purple dan silk was used; for the Censorate, Six Ministries, Imperial Clan Court, Commandery Office, and Inspection Office black slanted leather; for temples, directorates, various bureaus attending court, and prefectures and counties, all yellow leather; each seven cun long, two cun wide, and half a cun thick; all suspended from the bound belt; after leaving office suspended on informal dress; violators were corrected by the responsible office.

units.zh: 大定十三年，太常寺擬士人及僧尼道女冠有師號、並良閑官八品以上，許服花紗綾羅絲綢。
units.en: In the thirteenth year of Dading [1173], the Office of Imperial Sacrifices ruled that scholars, titled Buddhist and Daoist clergy, and good or leisure officials of eighth rank and above might wear floral gauze, damask, silk gauze, and silk.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dading, the Office of Imperial Sacrifices proposed that scholars and Buddhist monks and nuns, Daoist priests and nuns with master titles, and good and leisure officials eighth rank and above, were permitted to wear floral gauze, damask, silk gauze, and silk.

units.zh: 在官承應有出身人、帶八品以下官，未帶官亦同，許服花紗綾羅襜絲絲綢，家屬同，婦人許用珠為首飾。
units.en: Serving attendants with examination backgrounds, officials of eighth rank and below (including those not yet formally commissioned), might wear floral gauze, damask, dan silk, and silk, as could their families; women might use pearls in head ornaments.
units.literal: Serving attendants in office with examination backgrounds, officials bearing eighth rank and below, and those not yet bearing office were the same; permitted to wear floral gauze, damask, dan silk, and silk; families the same; women permitted to use pearls for head ornaments.

units.zh: 其都孔目與八品良閑官同，京府州縣司吏皆與庶人同。
units.en: Capital chief clerks followed eighth-rank good and leisure officials; capital, prefectural, and county clerks followed commoners.
units.literal: Capital chief clerks were the same as eighth-rank good and leisure officials; capital, prefectural, and county clerks were all the same as commoners.

units.zh: 庶人止許服霡綢、絹布、毛褐、花紗、無紋素羅、絲綿，其頭巾、系腰、領帕許用芝麻羅、絛用絨織成者，不得以金玉犀象諸寶瑪瑙玻璃之類為器皿、及裝飾刀把鞘、並銀裝釘床榻之類。
units.en: Commoners might wear only mist silk, silk cloth, woolens, floral gauze, plain gauze, and silk floss, with sesame gauze for headcloth, waist tie, and collar scarf and velvet-woven cords. They might not use gold, jade, rhinoceros, ivory, precious stones, agate, or glass for vessels, knife fittings, or silver-mounted bed furniture.
units.literal: Commoners were permitted only to wear mist silk, silk cloth, woolen cloth, floral gauze, unpatterned plain gauze, and silk floss; for headcloth, waist tie, and collar scarf sesame gauze was permitted; cords woven of velvet were permitted; they might not use gold, jade, rhinoceros, ivory, various treasures, agate, glass, and the like for vessels, or to ornament knife handles and scabbards, or silver-fitted nailed beds and couches.

units.zh: 婦人首飾，不許用珠翠鈿子等物，翠毛除許裝飾花環冠子，餘外並禁。
units.en: Women's head ornaments might not include pearls, kingfisher inlay, or similar pieces, except that kingfisher feathers were allowed on floral-wreath crowns; all else was forbidden.
units.literal: Women's head ornaments might not use pearls, kingfisher, inlay plaques, and the like; kingfisher feathers were excepted for ornamenting floral-wreath crowns; all else was forbidden.

units.zh: 兵卒許服無紋壓羅、霡綢、絹布、毛褐。
units.en: Soldiers and garrison troops might wear unpatterned pressed gauze, mist silk, silk cloth, or woolens.
units.literal: Soldiers and garrison troops were permitted unpatterned pressed gauze, mist silk, silk cloth, and woolen cloth.

units.zh: 奴婢止許服霡綢、絹布、毛褐。
units.en: Slaves might wear only mist silk, silk cloth, or woolens.
units.literal: Male and female slaves were permitted only mist silk, silk cloth, and woolen cloth.

units.zh: 倡優遇迎接、公筵承應，許暫服繪畫之服，其私服與庶人同。
units.en: Actors and entertainers might temporarily wear painted costumes when receiving guests or serving at public banquets, but their private dress matched commoners.
units.literal: Actors and entertainers when meeting receptions or attending public banquets in service were permitted temporarily to wear painted dress; their private dress was the same as commoners.

units.zh: 四年七月，上以諸路枷杖多不如法，平章政事守貞曰：「枷杖尺寸有制，提刑兩月一巡察，必不敢違法也。」
units.en: In the seventh month of the fourth year, noting that cangues and beating staves across the circuits often failed to meet statutory standards, Grand Counselor Shouzhen said: 'The dimensions of cangues and staves are prescribed by law, and investigative commissioners inspect every two months—officials will not dare violate the regulations.'
units.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, the emperor, because cangues and staffs in various circuits mostly did not accord with law, Grand Counselor Shouzhen said: 'Cangue and staff dimensions have regulation; investigative commissioners once every two months inspect—surely they dare not violate law.'

units.zh: 平章守貞曰：「是制自大定二十三年罷之。
units.en: Grand Counselor Shouzhen noted: 'That practice was abolished in the twenty-third year of Dading.
units.literal: Grand Counselor Shouzhen said: 'That system since Dading twenty-third year was abolished.

units.zh: 然律有起請諸條，是古亦許情見矣。」
units.en: Yet the statutes contain provisions for submitted petitions, which shows that discretionary views were permitted even in antiquity.'
units.literal: Yet statutes have petition-initiated articles—thus antiquity also permitted discretionary views.'

units.zh: 海陵天德四年，有司言：「燕京興建太廟，複立原廟。
units.en: In Hailing's fourth Tiande year, the responsible offices reported: "With the Grand Ancestral Temple rising in Yanjing, original shrines should be re-established as well.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tiande under Prince Hailing, the relevant offices stated: "The Grand Ancestral Temple is being built in Yanjing, and original temples are to be re-established.

units.zh: 舉冊官對舉冊，讀冊官中書令一拜起，跪，搢笏，讀冊文曰：「孝孫嗣皇帝臣某，謹拜手稽首奉玉冊玉寶，恭上尊諡曰應乾興運昭德定功睿神莊孝仁明大聖武元皇帝。」
units.en: The officials lifting the register held it between them; the reader, the Director of the Secretariat, bowed once, rose, knelt, inserted his tablet, and read the text of the register: 'The filial grandson, the succeeding emperor, your subject [name], reverently bows with joined hands and prostrates himself to present jade registers and jade seals, and reverently confers the posthumous title Emperor Yingqian Xingyun Zhaode Dinggong Ruishen Zhuangxiao Renming Dasheng Wuyuan.'
units.literal: The officials lifting the register held it facing each other; the official reading the register, the Director of the Secretariat, bowed once, rose, knelt, inserted his tablet, and read the text of the register: 'The filial grandson, the succeeding emperor, your subject [name], reverently bows with joined hands and prostrates himself to present jade registers and jade seals, and reverently confers the posthumous honorific title Responding to Heaven, Raising the Fortune, Illustrious in Virtue, Settling Merit, Sagely in Spirit, Solemn in Filial Piety, Benevolent and Bright, Great Sage Martial Primary Emperor.'

units.zh: 大定十九年，奉上孝成皇帝諡號。
units.en: In Dading 19 the court presented the posthumous title of Emperor Xiaocheng.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year of Dading, the honorific title of Emperor Xiaocheng was presented.

units.zh: 宜上諡號曰閔宗武靈皇帝。」
units.en: The posthumous title Emperor Minzong Wuling should be conferred.'
units.literal: The honorific title Emperor Minzong Wuling should be conferred.'

units.zh: 今擬增上閔宗尊諡曰弘基纘武莊靖孝成皇帝，仍加諡悼皇后曰悼平皇后。」
units.en: It is now proposed to augment Minzong's posthumous title to Emperor Hongji Zuowu Zhuangjing Xiaocheng, and to add for Empress Dao the title Empress Daoping.'
units.literal: It is now proposed to augment Minzong's honorific title to Emperor Hongji Zuowu Zhuangjing Xiaocheng, and to add for Empress Dao the title Empress Daoping.'

units.zh: 二十六年，敕再議閔宗廟號，禮官擬上「襄、威、敬、定、桓、烈、熙」七字，奉旨用「熙」字，乃以明年四月一日，遣官奏告太廟及閔宗本室，易新廟號。
units.en: In year 26 an edict ordered further deliberation on Minzong's temple name; ritual officials proposed seven characters—'xiang,' 'wei,' 'jing,' 'ding,' 'huan,' 'lie,' and 'xi'—and by imperial order 'xi' was chosen; on the first day of the fourth month of the following year officials were sent to announce at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and at Minzong's own chamber, adopting the new temple name.
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, an edict ordered further deliberation on Minzong's temple name; the ritual officials proposed seven characters—'xiang,' 'wei,' 'jing,' 'ding,' 'huan,' 'lie,' and 'xi'—and by imperial order the character 'xi' was adopted; on the first day of the fourth month of the following year officials were dispatched to present memorial announcements at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and at Minzong's own chamber, changing to the new temple name.

units.zh: 元年十一月十六日，詔曰：「前君乃太祖之長孫，受太宗之遺命，嗣膺神器，十有五年。
units.en: On the sixteenth day of the eleventh month of the first year an edict stated: 'The former ruler was the eldest grandson of Emperor Taizu; he received Emperor Taizong's testamentary mandate, succeeded to the throne, and reigned for fifteen years.
units.literal: On the sixteenth day of the eleventh month of the first year, an edict stated: 'The former ruler was the eldest grandson of Emperor Taizu; he received the testamentary mandate of Emperor Taizong, succeeded to the sacred vessel, and reigned for fifteen years.

units.zh: 十月三日，奉上尊諡冊寶儀：前期，有司供張辰居殿神禦床案。
units.en: On the third day of the tenth month the rite for presenting posthumous registers and seals was performed. Beforehand the relevant offices set out the spirit couch and table in Chenju Hall.
units.literal: On the third day of the tenth month, the rite for presenting posthumous honorific registers and seals: beforehand, the relevant offices set out the spirit couch and table in Chenju Hall.

units.zh: 晚雖淫刑，幾於恣意，冤施弟後，戮及良工，虐不及民，事猶可諫，過之至此，古或有焉。
units.en: In his later years he used excessive punishments and came near to acting at will—wrongfully punishing his younger brother's widow and killing worthy craftsmen—yet his cruelty did not reach the common people, and the matter could still be remonstrated against; that excess reached this point is something even the ancients sometimes did.
units.literal: In his later years, though he used excessive punishments and came near to acting at will—wrongfully punishing his younger brother's widow and killing worthy craftsmen—his cruelty did not reach the common people, and the matter could still be remonstrated against; that excess reached this point is something the ancients sometimes did.

units.zh: 右丞相岐國王亮不務弼諧，反行篡弑，妄加黜廢，抑損徽稱。
units.en: Chief Councillor on the right, Prince of Qi Liang, did not devote himself to harmonious assistance but instead carried out usurpation and regicide, recklessly imposing dismissal and degradation and diminishing the former ruler's posthumous title.
units.literal: The Chief Councillor on the right, Prince of Qi Liang, did not devote himself to harmonious assistance but instead carried out usurpation and regicide, recklessly imposing dismissal and degradation and diminishing the former ruler's honorific title.

units.zh: 垂拱仰成，委任勳戚，廢齊國以省徭賦，柔宋人而息兵戈，世格泰和，俗躋仁壽，混車書於南北，一尉候於東西。
units.en: He ruled by deferring to accomplished ministers, entrusted affairs to meritorious kinsmen, abolished the Qi state to lighten corvée and taxes, treated the Song people gently and stilled the weapons of war; the age attained great peace, customs rose to benevolence and longevity, chariots and books were united north and south, and frontier posts were made one from east to west.
units.literal: He ruled by deferring to accomplished ministers, entrusted affairs to meritorious kinsmen, abolished the Qi state to reduce corvée and taxes, treated the Song people gently and stilled the weapons of war; the age attained great peace, customs rose to benevolence and longevity, chariots and books were united north and south, and frontier posts were made one from east to west.

units.zh: 遠近傷嗟，神人憤怒，天方悔禍，朕乃繼興，受天下之樂推，居域中之有大。
units.en: Near and far mourned; spirits and men were enraged; Heaven was about to repent of the calamity, and I then succeeded, receiving the willing submission of all under Heaven and occupying the great position within the realm.
units.literal: Near and far mourned and sighed; spirits and men were enraged; Heaven was about to repent of the calamity, and I then succeeded and arose, receiving the willing submission of all under Heaven and occupying the great position within the realm.

units.zh: 將撥亂而反正，務在革非。
units.en: I shall quell disorder and restore rectitude, striving above all to reform what is wrong.
units.literal: I shall quell disorder and restore rectitude, striving above all to reform what is wrong.

units.zh: 期事亡以如存，聿思盡禮。
units.en: I expect to treat the dead as if they still lived and think constantly of fulfilling every rite.
units.literal: I expect to treat the dead as if they still lived and think constantly of fulfilling every rite.

units.zh: 執折上巾者升，掌冠者降一等受之，右執項，左執前，進皇太子席前，北向立，祝曰：“谘爾元子，肇冠於阼。
units.en: The attendant bearing the folded kerchief ascended. The crown-placer stepped down one level to receive it, grasping the rear with his right hand and the front with his left, and advanced to stand north-facing before the crown prince's seat. He pronounced the blessing: "I announce to you, eldest son, that you are first capped at the eastern steps.
units.literal: The bearer of the folded-up kerchief ascended; the crown-placer descended one step to receive it, holding the nape with his right hand and the front with his left, advanced before the crown prince's seat, stood facing north, and offered the blessing: "I announce to you, eldest son, that you are first capped at the eastern steps.

units.zh: 左輔詣御坐前，承製降東階，詣掌 冠者前西向稱有制，典儀讚在位官再拜訖，宣製曰：“皇太子冠，命卿等行禮。”
units.en: The Left Assistant approached the throne, received the edict, descended the eastern steps, and stood west-facing before the crown-placers to announce that an edict was forthcoming. After the master of ceremonies had the officials in attendance perform a double bow, the edict was read: "The crown prince is to receive his cap; I command you to conduct the ceremony."
units.literal: The Left Assistant went before the imperial seat, received the edict, descended the eastern steps, went before the crown-placers, faced west, and announced that there was an edict; the master of ceremonies had the officials in position double-bow; then the edict was proclaimed: "The crown prince is to be capped; I command you to perform the ceremony."

units.zh: 徽宗親製《冠禮沿革》十一卷，命儀禮局仿以編次。
units.en: Emperor Huizong personally compiled eleven fascicles entitled Evolution of Capping Rites and instructed the Bureau of Ceremonial to organize the ritual according to that model.
units.literal: Emperor Huizong personally composed eleven fascicles of "Evolution of Capping Rites," ordering the Bureau of Ceremonial to compile and arrange [the ceremony] according to it.

units.zh: 太子興，內侍跪進服，服訖，樂止。
units.en: The crown prince rose while inner attendants knelt to bring forward his garments. Once he was dressed, the music stopped.
units.literal: The crown prince rose; inner attendants knelt to present the garments; when he was dressed, the music ceased.

units.zh: 禮直官等引太子降自東階，樂作，由 西階升，即醴席南向坐，樂止。
units.en: Ritual officers escorted the crown prince down the eastern steps to music, then up the western steps to take his seat facing south at the ceremonial wine seat; the music stopped.
units.literal: Ritual officers and others led the crown prince down the eastern steps; music was performed; he ascended by the western steps and took his seat facing south at the ceremonial wine seat; the music ceased.

units.zh: 太常博士請再拜，太子 再拜訖，搢笏，舞蹈，再拜，奏聖躬萬福，又再拜。
units.en: An academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices called for a double bow. The crown prince completed it, inserted his tablet, performed the dance-bow and another double bow, reported that the Son of Heaven enjoyed ten thousand blessings, and bowed again.
units.literal: A Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician requested a double bow; the crown prince finished double-bowing, inserted his tablet, performed the dance-bow, double-bowed again, reported that the sacred person enjoyed ten thousand blessings, and double-bowed once more.

units.zh: 宣訖，太子再拜訖，禮直官等引太子前，俯伏，跪，奏稱：“臣雖不敏，敢不祗奉！”
units.en: When the proclamation ended, the crown prince completed his double bow. Ritual officers led him forward; he prostrated himself, knelt, and reported: "Though your servant is not clever, how dare he fail to obey reverently!"
units.literal: When the proclamation was finished, the crown prince finished double-bowing; ritual officers and others led the crown prince forward; he prostrated himself, knelt, and reported: "Though your servant is not clever, how dare he not reverently obey!"

units.zh: 太子入內，朝見皇后，如宮中儀。
units.en: The crown prince entered the inner palace and paid his respects to the empress according to the palace rites.
units.literal: The crown prince entered the inner quarters and paid his respects to the empress, as in the palace ceremony.

units.zh: 大晟展宮架樂於橫街南，太常設 太子冠席東階上、東宮官位於後，設褥位，陳服於席南，東領北上。
units.en: The Dasheng Music Office set up the palace frame orchestra south of the cross street. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices placed the crown prince's capping seat on the eastern steps, with positions for Eastern Palace officials behind it, a cushioned seat, and ceremonial dress laid out to the south of the seat, facing east with the leading edge to the north.
units.literal: The Dasheng Office deployed the palace frame music south of the cross street; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set the crown prince's capping seat on the eastern steps, with Eastern Palace officials' positions behind it; a cushioned seat was set out, and garments were displayed south of the seat, aligned east-leading north-up.

units.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人、太常博士引太子詣朵殿東房。
units.en: Ritual officers, Communication Chamber attendants, and academicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices escorted the crown prince to the eastern room of the side hall.
units.literal: Ritual officers, Communication Chamber attendants, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the crown prince to the eastern chamber of the side hall.

units.zh: 東宮官入，詣太子東房，次禮直官等引太子，內侍二人夾侍，東宮官後從，《欽安之樂》作，即席西向坐，樂止。
units.en: Eastern Palace officials entered and went to the crown prince's eastern room. Ritual officers then escorted the crown prince out, flanked by two inner attendants with Eastern Palace officials following behind, to the music of Qin'an. He took his seat facing west, and the music stopped.
units.literal: Eastern Palace officials entered and went to the crown prince's eastern chamber; next ritual officers and others led the crown prince, with two inner attendants attending on either side and Eastern Palace officials following behind; "Qin'an" music was performed; he took his seat facing west; the music ceased.

units.zh: 掌冠者揖太子復坐，禮直官等引掌冠者降詣罍洗，如上儀。
units.en: The crown-placer gestured for the crown prince to resume his seat, and ritual officers escorted him down to the wash basin as before.
units.literal: The crown-placer bowed to the crown prince to return to his seat; ritual officers and others led the crown-placer down to the jar and wash-basin, as in the preceding ceremony.

units.zh: 執遠遊冠者升，掌冠者降二等受之，右執項，左執前，進太子席前，北向立，祝曰：“爰即令辰，申加元服。
units.en: The attendant bearing the Cap of Distant Travels ascended. The crown-placer stepped down two levels to receive it, grasping the rear with his right hand and the front with his left, and advanced to stand north-facing before the crown prince's seat. He pronounced the blessing: "On this auspicious hour we confer the second cap.
units.literal: The bearer of the Cap of Distant Travels ascended; the crown-placer descended two steps to receive it, holding the nape with his right hand and the front with his left, advanced before the crown prince's seat, stood facing north, and offered the blessing: "On this auspicious hour we add the second cap.

units.zh: 太子興，內侍跪進服，服訖，樂止。
units.en: The crown prince rose while inner attendants knelt to bring forward his garments. Once he was dressed, the music stopped.
units.literal: The crown prince rose; inner attendants knelt to present the garments; when he was dressed, the music ceased.

units.zh: 掌冠者揖太子復坐，掌冠者降 詣罍洗，及讚冠者跪，脫遠遊冠，並如上儀。
units.en: The crown-placer gestured for the crown prince to resume his seat, then went down to the wash basin while the crown-praiser knelt to remove the Cap of Distant Travels, all as before.
units.literal: The crown-placer bowed to the crown prince to return to his seat; the crown-placer descended to the jar and wash-basin, and the crown-praiser knelt and removed the Cap of Distant Travels—all as in the preceding ceremony.

units.zh: 執袞冕者升，掌冠者降三等受之，右執項，左執前，進太子席前，北向立，祝曰：“三加彌尊，國本以正。
units.en: The attendant bearing the imperial robe-and-crown ascended. The crown-placer stepped down three levels to receive it and advanced to stand north-facing before the crown prince's seat. He pronounced the blessing: "With the third investiture ever more exalted, the foundation of the realm is secured.
units.literal: The bearer of the imperial robe-and-cap ascended; the crown-placer descended three steps to receive it, holding the nape with his right hand and the front with his left, advanced before the crown prince's seat, stood facing north, and offered the blessing: "With the third addition ever more honored, the foundation of the state is made right.

units.zh: 太子搢圭，跪受爵，《正安之樂》作，飲訖，奠爵執圭。
units.en: The crown prince inserted his tablet and knelt to receive the goblet as Zheng'an was played. When he had drunk, he set down the goblet and took up his tablet.
units.literal: The crown prince inserted his tablet, knelt to receive the goblet; "Zheng'an" music was performed; when he had drunk, he set down the goblet and held the tablet.

units.zh: 太官令設饌席前，太子搢圭，食訖，樂 止，執圭興，太官令徹饌、爵。
units.en: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen set food before the seat. The crown prince inserted his tablet and ate; when he had finished, the music stopped. He rose holding his tablet, and the Director removed the food and goblet.
units.literal: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen set food before the seat; the crown prince inserted his tablet, ate, and finished; the music ceased; he held the tablet and rose; the Director of the Imperial Kitchen removed the food and goblet.

units.zh: 〈（太子初行，樂作，至位，樂止。）〉
units.en: (When the crown prince first set out, music played; when he reached his station, it stopped.)
units.literal: (When the crown prince first set out, music was performed; when he reached his position, the music ceased.)

units.zh: 左輔承旨，降自東階，詣太子前，西向，宣曰“有敕”，太子再拜，宣敕曰：“事親以孝，接下以仁。
units.en: The Left Assistant received the command, descended the eastern steps, and stood west-facing before the crown prince to announce, "There is an edict." The crown prince double-bowed, and the edict was read: "Serve your parents with filial piety; treat your subordinates with benevolence.
units.literal: The Left Assistant received the command, descended the eastern steps, went before the crown prince, faced west, and announced, "There is an edict"; the crown prince double-bowed; the edict was proclaimed: "Serve your parents with filial piety; treat your subordinates with benevolence.

units.zh: 衛紹王諱永濟，小字興勝，更諱允濟，章宗時避顯宗諱，詔改「允」為「永」。
units.en: Wei Shaowang—taboo name Yongji, childhood name Xingsheng, once taboo-named Yunji—during Zhangzong's reign, because of the taboo on Xianzong's name, received an edict changing "Yun" to "Yong."
units.literal: Wei Shaowang, taboo name Yongji, childhood name Xingsheng, formerly taboo-named Yunji; during Zhangzong's reign, to avoid Xianzong's taboo, an edict changed "Yun" to "Yong."

units.zh: 二十九年，世宗崩，章宗即位，進封潞王。
units.en: In year 29 Shizong died and Zhangzong took the throne; he was advanced to Prince of Lu.
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Shizong died and Zhangzong ascended; he was advanced to Prince of Lu.

units.zh: 章宗崩，匡等傳遣詔，立衛王。
units.en: Zhangzong died; Kuang and his party passed on the final edict and set Prince Wei on the throne.
units.literal: Zhangzong died; Kuang and the others transmitted the death edict and enthroned Prince Wei.

units.zh: 既無繼嗣，而諸叔兄弟多在，章宗皆不肯立，惟欲立衛王，故於辭行留之。
units.en: He had no son, and many uncles and brothers still lived; Zhangzong would raise none of them, wishing only to make Prince Wei heir—so when Prince Wei tried to leave, he was kept back.
units.literal: With no heir of his own and many uncles and brothers still living, Zhangzong would establish none of them; he only wished to make Prince Wei his successor, and therefore detained him when he sought to leave.

units.zh: 而永蹈無後，乃以衛王子按陳為鄭王後，賜衛王詔曰：「朕念鄭王自棄天常，以幹國憲，槁瘞曠野，忽諸不祀。
units.en: Yongtao left no heir, so Prince Wei's son An Chen was made heir to Prince of Zheng. The edict to Prince Wei ran: "I think of Prince of Zheng, who threw away Heaven's law and breached the state's statutes, left to wither in the wild, and passed from sacrifice altogether.
units.literal: Yongtao had no heir, so the Prince of Wei's son An Chen was made successor to Prince of Zheng. An edict to Prince Wei said: "I reflect on Prince of Zheng, who abandoned Heaven's constants and violated state law, withered in burial on the open plain, gone suddenly without sacrifice.

units.zh: 歷歲既久，深用愴然。
units.en: Years have gone by, and grief weighs on me.
units.literal: Years have passed and I am deeply grieved.

units.zh: 親親之情。
units.en: Kinship tugs at the heart.
units.literal: The bonds of kin weigh upon me.

units.zh: 有懷難置。
units.en: I cannot set the feeling aside.
units.literal: My heart cannot find rest.

units.zh: 已詔追復舊爵，改葬如儀。
units.en: I have already ordered his old rank restored and a proper reburial.
units.literal: I have already ordered his former title restored and burial redone according to rite.

units.zh: 稽考古禮，以卿之子按陳為鄭王後，謹其祭祀，卿其悉之。」
units.en: By the ancient rites, your son An Chen is made heir to Prince of Zheng to keep his sacrifices—take full heed of this."
units.literal: Examining ancient rites, I make your son An Chen successor to Prince of Zheng to tend his sacrifices—see that you know this fully."

units.zh: 初，章宗誅鄭王永蹈、趙王永中，久，頗悔之。
units.en: At first Zhangzong had put Prince of Zheng Yongtao and Prince of Zhao Yongzhong to death; in time he came to regret it deeply.
units.literal: Initially Zhangzong had executed Prince of Zheng Yongtao and Prince of Zhao Yongzhong; after a long while he deeply regretted it.

units.zh: 是時，章宗已感嗽疾，衛王且辭行，而章宗意留之。
units.en: By then Zhangzong had fallen ill with a cough; Prince Wei was ready to depart, but Zhangzong meant to keep him at court.
units.literal: By then Zhangzong had contracted a coughing illness; Prince Wei was about to take leave, but Zhangzong intended to keep him.

units.zh: 宗章初年，雅愛諸王，置王傳府尉官以傳導德義。
units.en: Early in Zhangzong's reign he had loved his brothers dearly and set tutors and household officers in each prince's house to teach virtue.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhangzong's reign he had dearly loved the princes and appointed tutors and household officers in each princely establishment to convey moral teaching.

units.zh: 而衛王乃永蹈母弟，柔弱鮮智能，故章宗愛之。
units.en: Prince Wei was Yongtao's uterine younger brother—soft, ungifted, and mild—so Zhangzong held him dear.
units.literal: Prince Wei was Yongtao's younger brother by the same mother—gentle, weak, and little gifted—so Zhangzong favored him.

units.zh: 無何，章宗大漸，元妃李氏、黃門李新喜、平章政事完顏匡定策。
units.en: Soon Zhangzong was near death; Yuan Consort Li, palace attendant Li Xinxhi, and Grand Councilor Wanyan Kuang fixed the succession.
units.literal: Before long Zhangzong fell critically ill; Yuan Consort Li, Palace Attendant Li Xinxhi, and Grand Councilor Wanyan Kuang settled the plan.

units.zh: 壬辰，章宗內人范氏損其遣腹，以詔內外。
units.en: On renchen Zhangzong's inner woman Fan injured the child she bore for him; an edict told the court and the realm.
units.literal: On renchen Zhangzong's inner attendant Fan harmed the pregnancy she was carrying for him; an edict announced this within and without.

units.zh: 初，章宗遣詔：「內人有娠者兩人，生男則立為儲貳。」
units.en: Earlier Zhangzong had sent an edict: "Two inner women are with child; whichever bears a son shall be made heir."
units.literal: Initially Zhangzong had issued an edict: "Among inner women, two are pregnant; if a son is born he shall be made heir."

units.zh: 四月庚辰，殺章宗元妃李氏及承御賈氏。
units.en: In the fourth month, on gengchen, Zhangzong’s Primary Consort Li shi and Palace Woman Jia shi were put to death.
units.literal: Fourth month, on gengchen, Zhangzong’s Primary Consort Li shi and Palace Woman Jia shi were killed.

units.zh: 《章宗實錄》詳其前事，《宜宗實錄》詳其後事。
units.en: The Veritable Record of Zhangzong treats the earlier reign; the Veritable Record of Xuanzong treats what followed.
units.literal: The Veritable Record of Zhangzong details earlier matters; the Veritable Record of Xuanzong details later matters.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略·陶穀傳》：穀本姓唐，避晉祖諱改姓陶，蓋當時避諱之體如此。）〉
units.en: (The Biography of Tao Gu in Outline History of the Eastern Capital records that Gu's original surname was Tang and that he changed it to Tao to avoid the taboo of the Jin founder. Such was the practice of taboo avoidance at the time.)〉
units.literal: (Biography of Tao Gu in Outline History of the Eastern Capital: Gu's original surname was Tang; to avoid the taboo of the Jin founder he changed his surname to Tao. Such was the practice of taboo avoidance at the time.)〉

units.zh: 平章政事張萬公謂拜禮各便所習，不須改也，司空完顏襄曰：「今諸人衽發皆從本朝之制，宜從本朝拜禮，松言是也。」
units.en: Grand Councilor Zhang Wangong said each should use the bow convenient to what he is accustomed to and need not change; Minister of Works Wanyan Xiang said: "Now all people wear their hair according to our dynasty's regulation—they should follow the native-country court bow; Song's words are correct."
units.literal: Grand Councilor Zhang Wangong said each should use the bow convenient to what he is accustomed to and need not change; Minister of Works Wanyan Xiang said: "Now all people wear their hair according to our dynasty's regulation—they should follow the native-country court bow; Song's words are correct."

units.zh: 承安五年五月，上諭旨有司曰：「女直、漢人拜數可以相從者，酌中議之。」
units.en: In the fifth month of Chengan 5, the emperor instructed the responsible offices: "Where Jurchen and Han bowing counts can follow each other, deliberate and decide a middle course."
units.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Chengan, the emperor instructed the responsible offices: "Where Jurchen and Han bowing counts can follow each other, deliberate and decide a middle course."
